diff --git a/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh b/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh
index f9aa8c41..28684653 100755
--- a/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh
+++ b/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh
@@ -120,6 +120,649 @@
 # is exec'd only inside emit_block and the FR-SZ bypass audit branch).
 # =============================================================================
 
+# =============================================================================
+# FR-6 heredoc consumer classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1; knob
+# destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier, default true; false = the
+# pre-cycle scan, i.e. only the #1245 quoted-cat scrub below).
+# Defined BEFORE the bash-version guard and the stdin read so another script
+# can source this file with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 and call
+#   _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   → prints interpreter|nonexec|none
+#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>               → exit 0 iff nonexec
+# Bash 3.2 compatible (no ${x,,}, no mapfile, no associative arrays) and safe
+# under a caller's `set -u`.
+#
+# Grammar (literal command text; no alias or function expansion; CRLF folded
+# to LF). The command is walked line by line; a line holding an unquoted
+# `<<` / `<<-` (not `<<<`) is a heredoc header, the body runs to the first
+# line equal to the delimiter (leading tabs stripped for `<<-`). FULL SCAN
+# (the whole command as today) on: any other control character, a header the
+# tokenizer cannot read (open quote, trailing backslash, comment), more than
+# one heredoc on a header, a delimiter that is not a plain word ('W', "W",
+# \W or W with W in [A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]; `$X` is a variable delimiter), or a
+# missing terminator. Per heredoc the class is:
+#   interpreter — body scanned exactly as today: the header holds `$(`, a
+#     backtick, `<(` or `>(`, a paren or brace group or a shell keyword; it
+#     continues on the next line (`|`, `&&`, `||` last) or an earlier line
+#     opened a substitution, group, quote or pipe; a member of the heredoc's
+#     pipeline is a shell, interpreter, wrapper that runs its argument or SQL
+#     runner (_bdb_hd_is_interp, _bdb_hd_is_runner); an allowlisted form
+#     carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag (-c, -e, -x clusters, --exec,
+#     --eval, --command, in-place); a write target is executable content
+#     (_bdb_hd_exec_dest: script extension, .claude/hooks, .claude/settings*
+#     .json, .git/hooks, .git/config, rc/profile files, /etc, a bin dir or a
+#     directory on PATH, or any non-literal path); the first body line is a
+#     shebang; the body holds `<<` (nested); a target's basename appears
+#     elsewhere in the command outside the safe readers (_bdb_hd_same_line_exec:
+#     `bash x`, `./x`, `source x`, `. x`, `chmod +x x`, `exec x`, cp/mv …).
+#   nonexec — every pipeline member is an exact allowlisted form
+#     (_bdb_hd_member): cat, tee, printf, echo with plain-file or stdout sinks;
+#     gh pr|issue comment -F -; gh pr create --body-file -; git commit -F -;
+#     br create|update reading `-`; jq/yq without in-place; grep; sed -n with
+#     a print-only script; sort; wc. The body is then scanned PER SEGMENT
+#     (_bdb_hd_scan_body): each line split on ; && || | &, wrapper prefixes
+#     stripped (sudo command exec env nice time nohup builtin stdbuf ionice,
+#     a leading backslash, quote, paren or brace, assignments, an absolute
+#     path); a segment whose command word is a fence verb (rm git find dd
+#     mkfs* shred truncate kubectl terraform aws gcloud psql mysql DROP
+#     DELETE TRUNCATE) is kept on its own line for the normal rules, other
+#     segments are dropped. The body falls back to a full scan when it holds
+#     `$(`, a backtick, `<(` or `>(` under an unquoted delimiter, or a segment
+#     word is an interpreter or wrapper, or a variable (`$x -rf /`; such a
+#     segment is ALSO scanned as rm, git and kubectl with the same arguments).
+#     Special case (the #1245 scrub): a standalone quoted-delimiter `cat`
+#     whose header is exactly `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops the whole body.
+#   none — the consumer is on neither list: full scan.
+# Documented gap: a body written to a plain file by one command and executed
+# by a LATER command is outside a per-command fence (the Write tool shares it).
+# =============================================================================
+_bdb_hd_op_re='^[0-9]*(<<<|<<-|&>>|<<|>>|>[|]|&&|[|][|]|[|]&|&>|<>|>&[0-9-]*|<&[0-9-]*|;;|;|&|[|]|<|>|[(]|[)])$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dw='^[A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dsq="^'([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)'\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_ddq='^"([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)"$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dbs='^\\([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)$'
+_bdb_hd_re_psq="^'([^']*)'\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_pdq="^\"([^\"\$\`\\\\]*)\"\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_pbare="^[^'\"\$\`\\\\]+\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_ctl=$'[\x01-\x08\x0b-\x1f\x7f]'
+_bdb_hd_re_exflag='^-[A-Za-z]*[cex][A-Za-z]*$'
+_bdb_hd_re_exlong='^--(exec|eval|command|in-?place)'
+_bdb_hd_re_ext='\.(sh|bash|zsh|ksh|csh|fish|py|pyw|rb|pl|pm|js|mjs|cjs|ts|mts|cts|ps1|psm1|php|lua|tcl|command|bat|cmd)$'
+_bdb_hd_re_sys='(^|/)(\.claude/hooks(/|$)|\.claude/settings[^/]*\.json$|\.git/hooks(/|$)|\.git/config$|\.gitconfig$|\.ssh/rc$|\.config/(fish|zsh|bash|git)/|s?bin/[^/]+$)'
+_bdb_hd_re_rc='(^|/)\.(bashrc|bash_profile|bash_login|bash_logout|profile|zshrc|zshenv|zprofile|zlogin|zlogout|kshrc|mkshrc|cshrc|tcshrc|login|logout|envrc)$'
+_bdb_hd_re_sedp='^(([0-9]+|[$]|/[^/]*/)(,([0-9]+|[$]|/[^/]*/))?)?p$'
+_bdb_hd_re_assign='^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*='
+_bdb_hd_re_varw='^[$]([{]|[A-Za-z_])'
+_bdb_hd_re_knob='^[[:space:]]+heredoc_classifier:[[:space:]]*["'"'"']?([A-Za-z]+)["'"'"']?[[:space:]]*(#.*)?$'
+
+# Shells, interpreters and wrappers that run their argument or stdin.
+_bdb_hd_is_interp() {
+  case "$1" in
+    bash|sh|zsh|dash|ksh|mksh|ash|fish|csh|tcsh|busybox|python|python[0-9]*|pypy*|node|nodejs|deno|bun|ruby|irb|perl|php|lua|luajit|tclsh|wish|expect|pwsh|powershell|osascript|Rscript) return 0 ;;
+    eval|source|.|exec|command|builtin|time|awk|gawk|mawk|nawk|make|gmake|m4|ed|ex|vi|vim|nvim|gdb) return 0 ;;
+    sudo|doas|su|runuser|env|xargs|parallel|timeout|nohup|nice|ionice|setsid|stdbuf|chroot|unshare|nsenter|ssh|docker|podman|kubectl|find|watch|script) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+# The SQL runners of the FR-1.4/5/6 precondition (same list).
+_bdb_hd_is_runner() {
+  case "$1" in
+    psql|pgcli|mysql|mariadb|mysqlsh|sqlite3|sqlcmd|sqlplus|isql|usql|litecli|duckdb|clickhouse|clickhouse-client|cockroach|bq|wrangler|prisma|supabase|drizzle-kit|knex|sequelize|typeorm|flyway|liquibase|dbmate|goose|sqitch|rails|manage.py|artisan|alembic|dbt|atlas|mongosh|sqlx) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+# Command words the fence's own rules match.
+_bdb_hd_is_destructive() {
+  case "$1" in
+    rm|git|find|dd|shred|truncate|kubectl|terraform|aws|gcloud|psql|mysql|mkfs|mkfs.*) return 0 ;;
+    [Dd][Rr][Oo][Pp]|[Dd][Ee][Ll][Ee][Tt][Ee]|[Tt][Rr][Uu][Nn][Cc][Aa][Tt][Ee]) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+# Readers that may name a heredoc's target elsewhere on the line.
+_bdb_hd_is_safe_reader() {
+  case "$1" in
+    cat|ls|wc|head|tail|grep|egrep|fgrep|rg|diff|cmp|stat|file|test|'['|echo|printf|sort|uniq|jq|yq|git|gh|br|mkdir|touch|realpath|readlink|basename|dirname|du|md5sum|sha1sum|sha256sum|shasum|b2sum|cksum) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_tokenize <line> → _bdb_hd_tok[] (words keep their quotes; operators
+# are separate tokens, an fd number joins its redirect). Returns 1 when the
+# line cannot be read: open quote, trailing backslash, unquoted comment.
+_bdb_hd_tokenize() {
+  local s="${1:-}" n i=0 ch tok="" q="" have=0 op cand
+  n=${#s}
+  _bdb_hd_tok=()
+  while (( i < n )); do
+    ch="${s:i:1}"
+    if [[ -n "$q" ]]; then
+      tok="$tok$ch"
+      if [[ "$q" == "'" ]]; then
+        [[ "$ch" == "'" ]] && q=""
+      elif [[ "$ch" == '\' ]]; then
+        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
+        i=$((i + 1)); tok="$tok${s:i:1}"
+      elif [[ "$ch" == '"' ]]; then
+        q=""
+      fi
+      i=$((i + 1)); continue
+    fi
+    case "$ch" in
+      "'"|'"') q="$ch"; tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      '\')
+        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
+        tok="$tok$ch${s:i+1:1}"; have=1; i=$((i + 2)) ;;
+      ' '|$'\t')
+        if (( have )); then _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"; tok=""; have=0; fi
+        i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      '#')
+        (( have )) || return 1
+        tok="$tok$ch"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      ';'|'&'|'|'|'<'|'>'|'('|')')
+        op=""
+        for cand in '<<<' '<<-' '&>>' '<<' '>>' '>|' '&&' '||' '|&' '&>' '<>' '>&' '<&' ';;' ';' '&' '|' '<' '>' '(' ')'; do
+          if [[ "${s:i:${#cand}}" == "$cand" ]]; then op="$cand"; break; fi
+        done
+        i=$((i + ${#op}))
+        if [[ "$op" == '>&' || "$op" == '<&' ]]; then
+          while (( i < n )) && [[ "${s:i:1}" == [0-9-] ]]; do op="$op${s:i:1}"; i=$((i + 1)); done
+        fi
+        if (( have )); then
+          if [[ "$tok" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$op" == '<'* || "$op" == '>'* ]]; then
+            op="$tok$op"
+          else
+            _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
+          fi
+          tok=""; have=0
+        fi
+        _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$op" ;;
+      *) tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+    esac
+  done
+  [[ -z "$q" ]] || return 1
+  (( have )) && _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
+  return 0
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_unq_path <word> → _hd_up; returns 1 for a non-literal path (an
+# expansion, an escape, mixed quoting) or an empty one.
+_bdb_hd_unq_path() {
+  _hd_up=""
+  if [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_psq ]] || [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pdq ]]; then
+    _hd_up="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
+  elif [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pbare ]]; then
+    _hd_up="$1"
+  else
+    return 1
+  fi
+  [[ -n "$_hd_up" ]]
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_exec_dest <unquoted path> → 0 when a write there is executable
+# content (or cannot be judged).
+_bdb_hd_exec_dest() {
+  local p="${1:-}" d e b old_ifs
+  case "$p" in
+    *'*'*|*'?'*|*'['*|*'{'*|'~'|'~'[!/]*|'') return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  [[ "$p" == '~/'* ]] && p="${HOME:-}/${p#'~/'}"
+  b="${p##*/}"
+  [[ "$b" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ext ]] && return 0
+  [[ "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_sys || "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_rc ]] && return 0
+  [[ "$p" == /etc/* ]] && return 0
+  if [[ "$p" == /* ]]; then d="${p%/*}"; [[ -n "$d" ]] || d="/"
+  elif [[ "$p" == */* ]]; then d="${PWD:-.}/${p%/*}"
+  else d="${PWD:-.}"
+  fi
+  old_ifs="$IFS"; IFS=':'
+  for e in ${PATH:-}; do
+    [[ -z "$e" || "$e" == "." ]] && e="${PWD:-.}"
+    [[ "$e" != "/" ]] && e="${e%/}"
+    if [[ "$d" == "$e" ]]; then IFS="$old_ifs"; return 0; fi
+  done
+  IFS="$old_ifs"
+  return 1
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_member <tokens…> → _hd_mcls (interpreter|nonexec|none) for one
+# pipeline member; write targets are appended to _hd_dests.
+_bdb_hd_member() {
+  local -a toks argv
+  local t nxt i n stdout_files=0 a0 base fd stdin=0 ops=0 want="" has_n=0 script=""
+  toks=("$@"); n=${#toks[@]}; argv=()
+  _hd_mcls=none
+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
+    t="${toks[i]}"
+    if [[ "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_op_re ]]; then
+      case "$t" in
+        *'<<<') return ;;
+        *'<<'|*'<<-') i=$((i + 1)); continue ;;
+        *'>&'[0-9]*|*'>&-'|*'<&'*) continue ;;
+        *'>'|*'>>'|*'>|'|*'>&'|'&>'|'&>>')
+          nxt="${toks[i+1]:-}"; i=$((i + 1))
+          if [[ -z "$nxt" || "$nxt" =~ $_bdb_hd_op_re ]]; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
+          _bdb_hd_unq_path "$nxt" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
+          case "$_hd_up" in /dev/null|/dev/stdout|/dev/stderr) continue ;; esac
+          _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up"
+          fd="${t%%[>&]*}"
+          [[ -z "$fd" || "$fd" == 1 || "$t" == '&>'* || "$t" == '>&' ]] && stdout_files=$((stdout_files + 1))
+          continue ;;
+        *) return ;;
+      esac
+    fi
+    argv[${#argv[@]}]="$t"
+  done
+  (( ${#argv[@]} > 0 )) || return
+  a0="${argv[0]}"
+  base="${a0#\\}"; base="${base##*/}"
+  if _bdb_hd_is_interp "$base" || _bdb_hd_is_runner "$base"; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
+  [[ "$a0" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*$ ]] || return
+  (( stdout_files <= 1 )) || return
+  for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+    t="${argv[i]}"
+    if [[ "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_exflag || "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_exlong ]]; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
+  done
+  case "$a0" in
+    cat)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do [[ "${argv[i]}" == "-" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; done ;;
+    tee)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          -a|--append|-p) ;;
+          -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
+          *) _bdb_hd_unq_path "$t" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
+             _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up" ;;
+        esac
+      done ;;
+    echo|printf)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        case "${argv[i]}" in -n|-E) ;; -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;; esac
+      done ;;
+    gh)
+      case "${argv[1]:-} ${argv[2]:-}" in
+        "pr comment"|"issue comment") want=" -F --body-file -R --repo |" ;;
+        "pr create") want=" -F --body-file --title -t --base -B --head -H --repo -R --label -l --reviewer -r --assignee -a --milestone -m --project -p --template -T | --draft -d --fill --fill-first --fill-verbose --no-maintainer-edit --dry-run " ;;
+        *) return ;;
+      esac
+      for ((i = 3; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          --body-file=-) stdin=1 ;;
+          --*=*) [[ "${want%%|*}" == *" ${t%%=*} "* ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+          -*)
+            if [[ "${want%%|*}" == *" $t "* ]]; then
+              i=$((i + 1))
+              [[ ( "$t" == "-F" || "$t" == "--body-file" ) && "${argv[i]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1
+            elif [[ "${want#*|}" != *" $t "* ]]; then
+              _hd_mcls=interpreter; return
+            fi ;;
+          *) ops=$((ops + 1)); [[ "${argv[2]}" == comment && $ops -le 1 ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+        esac
+      done
+      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+    git)
+      [[ "${argv[1]:-}" == commit ]] || return
+      for ((i = 2; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          -F|--file) i=$((i + 1)); [[ "${argv[i]:-}" == "-" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; stdin=1 ;;
+          --file=-|-F-) stdin=1 ;;
+          -q|--quiet|-s|--signoff|-a|--all|--allow-empty|--allow-empty-message|-v|--verbose|--no-edit|--amend) ;;
+          *) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
+        esac
+      done
+      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+    br)
+      case "${argv[1]:-}" in create|update) ;; *) return ;; esac
+      for ((i = 2; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          -d|--description|--body) [[ "${argv[i+1]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1 ;;
+          -f|--file) [[ "${argv[1]}" == create && "${argv[i+1]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1 ;;
+          --description=-|--body=-) stdin=1 ;;
+        esac

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# heredoc-classifier.sh — library entry points for the FR-6 heredoc consumer
     3	# classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1). The single implementation lives in the fence,
     4	# .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh; this file sources it in
     5	# library mode (BDB_LIB_ONLY=1, which the fence honours only when sourced) so
     6	# other scripts — guard-yield.sh's likely-false-positive heuristic — can call:
     7	#
     8	#   heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   prints interpreter|nonexec|none
     9	#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>          exit 0 iff the command's heredocs
    10	#                                           all have non-executing consumers
    11	#
    12	# Source only; never execute. Bash 3.2 compatible. When the fence cannot be
    13	# read the functions report "none" / exit 1, which callers treat as "no
    14	# classifier" (guard-yield.sh falls back to `<<` presence).
    15	_hc_lib_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    16	_hc_fence="${_hc_lib_dir}/../../hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
    17	if [[ -r "$_hc_fence" ]]; then
    18	  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    19	  BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 source "$_hc_fence"
    20	fi
    21	unset _hc_lib_dir _hc_fence
    22	
    23	heredoc_consumer_class() {
    24	  if declare -F _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    25	    _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}"
    26	  else
    27	    printf 'none\n'
    28	  fi
    29	}
    30	
    31	heredoc_nonexec() {
    32	  [[ "$(heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
    33	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh — Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes),
3	# per-task diff size (#961 K-1 / FR-1; reworked by cycle-129 D-4.3, D-4.2a,
4	# DEC-0141).
5	#
6	# PostToolUse:Write|Edit|NotebookEdit hook. Counts the lines each write adds
7	# (Write → content, Edit/NotebookEdit → new_string) and keeps a running total
8	# PER TASK:
9	#
10	#   key      the current task from `run-checkpoint.sh read --json`
11	#            (`.checkpoint.task`, else the sprint), else the session id from
12	#            the hook payload (`.session_id`, else LOA_SESSION_ID, else
13	#            <user>-<UTC date>); sanitised to ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (any other
14	#            byte becomes `_`, a leading dot becomes `_`, cut to 128 bytes)
15	#   state    .run/karpathy-surgical/<key>.jsonl — one small file per task, so
16	#            the total resets when the task changes; the directory keeps the
17	#            20 most recently written files and deletes older ones
18	#   summary  .run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json
19	#            {task, lines, threshold, over, updated_at}, rewritten atomically
20	#            after each counted write; the review's SURGICAL axis reads it
21	#   legacy   .run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl (the old session-long total) and
22	#            its two perf caches are deleted on the first run of this layout
23	#
24	# Over `karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task` (default 100) it prints the
25	# `[karpathy-surgical-warn]` stderr line and appends a trajectory event
26	# (karpathy-check.payload.schema.json). Non-blocking: always exits 0. The
27	# master switch `karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning` is read through
28	# loa_knob (explicit key, else the loa.profile default; `lean` turns it off).
29	#
30	# Safety (NFR-Sec-1): tool_input.content / new_string never reach state,
31	# summary or trajectory — only line counts, the file path (JSON-encoded by
32	# jq) and the sanitised key. Missing jq or yq, a missing config or a
33	# malformed payload is a silent no-op. A symlinked state directory or state
34	# file is not written through.
35	#
36	# Seams (tests): LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE (config), KARPATHY_STATE_DIR,
37	# KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE, KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE, KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR,
38	# KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD (default .claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh, which
39	# itself honours LOA_RUN_DIR), KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP (default 20).
40	#
41	# Design note: the session-long state file grew without bound, which is what
42	# the earlier perf passes (config-token and state-aggregate caches) existed
43	# to absorb. Per-task files are small and rotated, so the hook reads them in
44	# full each time and those caches are gone.
45	
46	set -uo pipefail
47	umask 077
48	export LC_ALL=C
49	
50	_src="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
51	_src_dir="${_src%/*}"
52	[[ "$_src_dir" == "$_src" ]] && _src_dir="."
53	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$_src_dir" && pwd)"
54	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"
55	DEFAULT_CONFIG="$REPO_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
56	CONFIG="${LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE:-$DEFAULT_CONFIG}"
57	DEFAULT_STATE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-surgical"
58	STATE_DIR="${KARPATHY_STATE_DIR:-$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR}"
59	SUMMARY="${KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json}"
60	LEGACY="${KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl}"
61	TRAJ_DIR="${KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR:-$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory}"
62	CHECKPOINT="${KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD:-$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh}"
63	KEEP="${KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP:-20}"
64	[[ "$KEEP" =~ ^[0-9]{1,4}$ && "$KEEP" -ge 1 ]] || KEEP=20
65

658	      (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
659	      i=$((i + 1)); continue
660	    fi
661	    _bdb_hd_header "$l"
662	    if (( _hd_ops == 0 )); then
663	      out="$out$l"$'\n'
664	      (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
665	      i=$((i + 1)); continue
666	    fi
667	    if (( _hd_ops != 1 )); then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
668	    found=-1
669	    for ((j = i + 1; j < _bdb_hd_n; j++)); do
670	      d="${_bdb_hd_L[j]}"
671	      if (( _hd_tabs )); then while [[ "$d" == $'\t'* ]]; do d="${d#$'\t'}"; done; fi
672	      if [[ "$d" == "$_hd_delim" ]]; then found=$j; break; fi
673	    done
674	    if (( found < 0 )); then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
675	    cls="$_hd_cls"
676	    (( ctx )) && cls=interpreter
677	    _hd_pipe_saved="$_hd_pipe"
678	    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]]; then
679	      first="${_bdb_hd_L[i+1]:-}"
680	      (( i + 1 < found )) || first=""
681	      first="${first#"${first%%[![:blank:]]*}"}"
682	      [[ "$first" == '#!'* ]] && cls=interpreter
683	    fi
684	    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]]; then
685	      local -a dests
686	      dests=(${_hd_dests[@]+"${_hd_dests[@]}"})
687	      for d in ${dests[@]+"${dests[@]}"}; do
688	        if _bdb_hd_exec_dest "$d" || _bdb_hd_same_line_exec "${d##*/}" "$i" $((i + 1)) $((found - 1)); then
689	          cls=interpreter; break
690	        fi
691	      done
692	    fi
693	    _bdb_hd_scan_body $((i + 1)) $((found - 1)) "$_hd_quoted"
694	    out="$out$l"$'\n'
695	    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]] && (( ! _hd_full )); then
696	      # #1245 special case: a standalone quoted `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops it all.

700	    else
701	      [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]] && cls=interpreter

703	      out="$out$_hd_synth"
704	    fi
705	    out="$out${_bdb_hd_L[found]}"$'\n'
706	    (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
707	    case "$cls" in
708	      interpreter) seen=interpreter ;;
709	      none) [[ "$seen" == interpreter ]] || seen=none ;;
710	      nonexec) [[ -n "$seen" ]] || seen=nonexec ;;
711	    esac
712	    i=$((found + 1))
713	  done
714	  _bdb_hd_class="${seen:-none}"
715	  printf '%s' "${out%$'\n'}"
716	}
717	
718	# The #1245 header grammar (byte-identical to _bdb_scrub_cat_heredoc's).
719	_bdb_hd_plain_cat() {
720	  local header="${1:-}" marker candidate
721	  local delimiter_re="<<(-?)('([[:alnum:]_]+)'|\"([[:alnum:]_]+)\")"
722	  local path_re="([[:alnum:]_./-]+|'[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+'|\"[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+\")"
723	  local header_re="^[[:blank:]]*cat[[:blank:]]+(HEREDOC([[:blank:]]+>>?[[:blank:]]*${path_re})?|>>?[[:blank:]]*${path_re}[[:blank:]]+HEREDOC)[[:blank:]]*$"

725	  marker="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"
726	  candidate="${header/"$marker"/HEREDOC}"
727	  [[ "$candidate" =~ $header_re ]]

729	
730	# Knob: destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier in the repo's
731	# .loa.config.yaml (read once, no fork, only for commands holding `<<`).
732	# Only an explicit false|no|off turns it off; turning it off only tightens.
733	_bdb_heredoc_knob_on() {
734	  local cfg="${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}}/.loa.config.yaml" content="" l in_blk=0
735	  [[ -f "$cfg" && -r "$cfg" ]] || return 0
736	  IFS= read -r -d '' content < "$cfg" || true
737	  [[ "$content" == *heredoc_classifier* ]] || return 0

739	    case "$l" in
740	      destructive_command_guard:*) in_blk=1; continue ;;
741	      [A-Za-z_]*) in_blk=0; continue ;;
742	    esac
743	    if (( in_blk )) && [[ "$l" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_knob ]]; then
744	      case "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" in false|False|FALSE|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) return 1 ;; esac
745	    fi
746	  done <<< "$content"
747	  return 0
748	}
749	
750	# Exported entry points (source with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1).
751	_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class() {
752	  local LC_ALL=C
753	  _bdb_heredoc_scrub "${1:-}" >/dev/null
754	  printf '%s\n' "$_bdb_hd_class"
755	}
756	heredoc_nonexec() {
757	  [[ "$(_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
758	}
759	
760	# Library mode: only when SOURCED. Executed with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 the hook runs
761	# normally — an environment variable can never switch the fence off.
762	if [[ "${BDB_LIB_ONLY:-}" == "1" && "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" != "${0:-}" ]]; then
763	  return 0
764	fi
765	
766	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
767	# jq presence probe (SDD §6.5 — SKP-008 mitigation, not full fix).
768	# If jq is absent, the input parse on line ~120 returns empty → existing
769	# fail-open guard exits 0. v1.38.0 adds a one-shot stderr WARNING so the
770	# operator / agent sees the safety guard is disabled this session.
771	# Tracked as cycle-112 candidate (filesystem-marker variant for cross-
772	# invocation persistence; env-var doesn't propagate across hook subprocess
773	# invocations per Flatline SKP-002 round-3 finding).
774	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
775	# perf pass-11 (skill-loop, 2026-07-06): HIGH-002 fix (BB review of PR #1176).
776	# Passes 2 & 8 introduced bash-4-only constructs into this fence (${x,,}
777	# case-folding, `mapfile`); pre-loop it was bash-3.2-portable (echo|grep -i).
778	# macOS ships bash 3.2. This guard runs BEFORE any bash-4 expansion executes
779	# (bash 3.2 defers ${,,} validation and the mapfile builtin lookup to runtime,
780	# so a runtime guard at the first executable line runs first and never reaches
781	# them). If a bash >=4 exists (the framework already requires it — beads-health
782	# etc. source bash-version-guard.sh), re-exec under it; stdin (the hook payload)
783	# and argv survive exec. Otherwise FAIL CLOSED (exit 2 = block): a
784	# destructive-command fence must never silently allow when it cannot evaluate.
785	# The generic bash-version-guard.sh exits 1, which is a NON-blocking PreToolUse
786	# hook error (fail-OPEN) — wrong direction for this hook, hence the inline form.
787	if [ "${BASH_VERSINFO:-0}" -lt 4 ]; then
788	    for _bh_cand in /opt/homebrew/bin/bash /usr/local/bin/bash /usr/bin/bash bash; do
789	        if command -v "$_bh_cand" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
790	            _bh_major="$("$_bh_cand" -c 'echo "${BASH_VERSINFO:-0}"' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
791	            if [ "${_bh_major:-0}" -ge 4 ]; then exec "$_bh_cand" "$0" "$@"; fi
792	        fi
793	    done
794	    echo "[block-destructive-bash] BLOCKED: bash >=4 required to evaluate the destructive-command fence (found ${BASH_VERSION:-unknown}); refusing to run degraded rather than allow a command unchecked. Install bash>=4 (macOS: brew install bash)." >&2
795	    exit 2
796	fi
797	
798	if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
799	  if [[ -z "${LOA_BLOCK_DESTRUCTIVE_JQ_MISSING_WARNED:-}" ]]; then
800	    echo "WARNING: block-destructive-bash: jq not in PATH — destructive-command pattern matching is DISABLED for this session. Install jq to restore safety guards." >&2

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.3
# (AC-2.3; PRD AC-4.3; SDD D-4.3, D-4.2a; DEC-0141)
#
# The surgical-diff hook keys its running total on the checkpoint task
# (`run-checkpoint.sh read --json`), else the sprint, else the session id;
# keeps one sanitised file per task under the state directory (at most 20);
# deletes the legacy session-long file; writes the summary the review's
# SURGICAL axis reads; and is silent when the knob is off. A fixture
# checkpoint (LOA_RUN_DIR) and a fake `br` on PATH stand in for a live run.
# =============================================================================

bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0

setup() {
    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    HOOK="$R/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh"
    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not available"
    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not available"
    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
    export LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$T/config.yaml"
    export KARPATHY_STATE_DIR="$T/state"
    export KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE="$T/summary.json"
    export KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE="$T/karpathy-task-state.jsonl"
    export KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR="$T/trajectory"
    export LOA_RUN_DIR="$T/run"
    unset LOA_SESSION_ID LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE
    mkdir -p "$T/run" "$T/bin"
    printf 'karpathy_principles:\n  surgical_diff_warning: true\n  diff_lines_per_task: 5\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
    # Fake beads: every bead reports closed unless BR_STATUS says otherwise.
    printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'printf "{\"status\":\"%s\"}\n" "${BR_STATUS:-closed}"' > "$T/bin/br"
    chmod +x "$T/bin/br"
    export PATH="$T/bin:$PATH"
}

# checkpoint <sprint> [task] — a schema-2 run state with that checkpoint
checkpoint() {
    jq -n --arg s "$1" --arg t "${2:-}" \
        '{schema_version: 2, state: "RUNNING",
          checkpoint: {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: "IMPLEMENT", ts: "2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"}}' \
        > "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json"
}

# write_lines <n> [session_id] — one Write payload adding n lines
write_lines() {
    local n="$1" sid="${2:-sess-1}" content
    content=$(seq 1 "$n" | paste -sd'\n' -)
    jq -nc --arg c "$content" --arg s "$sid" \
        '{tool_name: "Write", session_id: $s, tool_input: {file_path: "/repo/src/x.sh", content: $c}}' \
        | bash "$HOOK"
}

@test "KS-1 the counter resets when the checkpoint task changes" {
    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-aaa
    write_lines 3
    write_lines 2
    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "bd-aaa" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "5" ]
    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-bbb
    write_lines 2
    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "bd-bbb" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "2" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.over' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "false" ]
    [ "$(wc -l < "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-aaa.jsonl")" -eq 2 ]
    [ "$(wc -l < "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-bbb.jsonl")" -eq 1 ]
    [ "$(tail -1 "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-aaa.jsonl" | jq -r '.running_total')" = "5" ]
}

@test "KS-2 with no run in progress the key is the payload's session id, then LOA_SESSION_ID" {
    write_lines 1 "abc-123"
    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/abc-123.jsonl" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "abc-123" ]
    jq -nc '{tool_name: "Edit", tool_input: {file_path: "/repo/a", old_string: "", new_string: "x\ny"}}' \
        | LOA_SESSION_ID=env-sess bash "$HOOK"
    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/env-sess.jsonl" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "2" ]
}

@test "KS-3 a checkpoint whose task is still open in beads keys on the sprint" {
    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-open
    BR_STATUS=open write_lines 2
    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/sprint-256.jsonl" ]
    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-open.jsonl" ]
    # A sprint-granularity checkpoint (no task) keys on the sprint too.
    checkpoint sprint-257
    write_lines 1
    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "sprint-257" ]
}

@test "KS-4 the summary carries exactly task, lines, threshold, over, updated_at after each write" {
    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-sum
    write_lines 4
    run jq -c 'keys' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE"
    [ "$output" = '["lines","over","task","threshold","updated_at"]' ]
    jq -e '.task == "bd-sum" and .lines == 4 and .threshold == 5 and .over == false
           and (.updated_at | test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:]{8}Z$"))' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE" >/dev/null
    run --separate-stderr write_lines 3
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    jq -e '.lines == 7 and .over == true' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE" >/dev/null
    # The stderr warning keeps its wording.
    [[ "$stderr" == "[karpathy-surgical-warn] Session diff total 7 lines exceeds threshold 5. Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes): verify every changed line traces to the stated task. State: $KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-sum.jsonl" ]]
    ls "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE".tmp.* >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 1
    true
}

@test "KS-5 the state directory keeps the 20 most recently written task files" {
    mkdir -p "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR"
    local i
    for i in $(seq -w 1 25); do
        echo '{"lines_changed":1}' > "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-old-$i.jsonl"
        touch -d "2026-01-01 00:00:$i" "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-old-$i.jsonl"
    done
    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-new
    write_lines 1
    [ "$(ls "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR"/*.jsonl | wc -l)" -eq 20 ]
    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-new.jsonl" ]
    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-old-25.jsonl" ]
    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-old-06.jsonl" ]
    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-old-01.jsonl" ]
}

@test "KS-6 the legacy session-long state file is deleted on the first run" {
    printf '{"lines_changed":900,"running_total":900}\n' > "$KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE"
    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-leg
    write_lines 1
    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE" ]
    # The legacy total does not leak into the new layout.
    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "1" ]
}

@test "KS-7 task names are sanitised to ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\$ and stay inside the state directory" {
    checkpoint sprint-256 'bd-1'
    jq '.checkpoint.task = "Task 2.3: ../../evil\nname"' "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json" > "$T/s" && mv "$T/s" "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json"
    write_lines 1
    run ls -A "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR"
    [ "${#lines[@]}" -eq 1 ]
    [[ "${lines[0]}" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\.jsonl$ ]]
    [ "${lines[0]}" = "Task_2.3__.._.._evil_name.jsonl" ]
    [ "$(find "$T" -name '*evil*' | wc -l)" -eq 1 ]
    # A leading dot cannot make a hidden (unrotated) file.
    jq '.checkpoint.task = ".hidden"' "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json" > "$T/s" && mv "$T/s" "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json"
    write_lines 1
    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/_hidden.jsonl" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "_hidden" ]
}

@test "KS-8 knob off is silent: no state, no summary, no stderr" {
    printf 'karpathy_principles:\n  surgical_diff_warning: false\n  diff_lines_per_task: 1\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
    printf 'x\n' > "$KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE"
    run --separate-stderr write_lines 9
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ -z "$output" ] && [ -z "$stderr" ]
    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR" ] && [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE" ]
    # The `lean` profile turns it off without the key; an explicit true wins over lean.
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\nkarpathy_principles:\n  diff_lines_per_task: 1\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
    run --separate-stderr write_lines 9
    [ -z "$stderr" ] && [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE" ]
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\nkarpathy_principles:\n  surgical_diff_warning: true\n  diff_lines_per_task: 1\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# Issue #961 K-1 — Karpathy surgical-diff hook
# =============================================================================
# Pins the contract for .claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:
# fires `[karpathy-surgical-warn]` stderr line + trajectory event when the
# session diff accumulator exceeds `karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task`,
# while remaining non-blocking (always exits 0) per v1 invariant.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
    REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    HOOK="$REPO_ROOT/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh"
    [[ -x "$HOOK" ]] || skip "hook not executable"
    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not available"
    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not available"

    TMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"
    # cycle-129 D-4.3: per-task state under KARPATHY_STATE_DIR; with no run in
    # progress (empty LOA_RUN_DIR) the key is the session id.
    export KARPATHY_STATE_DIR="$TMP_DIR/state"
    export KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE="$TMP_DIR/summary.json"
    export KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE="$TMP_DIR/legacy-task-state.jsonl"
    export LOA_RUN_DIR="$TMP_DIR/run"
    export LOA_SESSION_ID="test-session"
    KARPATHY_TASK_STATE="$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/test-session.jsonl"
    export KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR="$TMP_DIR/trajectory"
    export LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$TMP_DIR/config.yaml"

    # Default test config — surgical_diff_warning on, threshold deliberately
    # tiny so we can trip it with a few small Write calls.
    cat > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE" <<EOF
karpathy_principles:
  surgical_diff_warning: true
  diff_lines_per_task: 5
  enforce: warn
EOF
}

teardown() {
    rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"
}

_write_input() {
    local content="$1"

_edit_input() {

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# heredoc-classifier.sh — library entry points for the FR-6 heredoc consumer
+# classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1). The single implementation lives in the fence,
+# .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh; this file sources it in
+# library mode (BDB_LIB_ONLY=1, which the fence honours only when sourced) so
+# other scripts — guard-yield.sh's likely-false-positive heuristic — can call:
+#
+#   heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   prints interpreter|nonexec|none
+#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>          exit 0 iff the command's heredocs
+#                                           all have non-executing consumers
+#
+# Source only; never execute. Bash 3.2 compatible. When the fence cannot be
+# read the functions report "none" / exit 1, which callers treat as "no
+# classifier" (guard-yield.sh falls back to `<<` presence).
+_hc_lib_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+_hc_fence="${_hc_lib_dir}/../../hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
+if [[ -r "$_hc_fence" ]]; then
+  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
+  BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 source "$_hc_fence"
+fi
+unset _hc_lib_dir _hc_fence
+
+heredoc_consumer_class() {
+  if declare -F _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}"
+  else
+    printf 'none\n'
+  fi
+}
+
+heredoc_nonexec() {
+  [[ "$(heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# heredoc-classifier.sh — library entry points for the FR-6 heredoc consumer
+# classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1). The single implementation lives in the fence,
+# .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh; this file sources it in
+# library mode (BDB_LIB_ONLY=1, which the fence honours only when sourced) so
+# other scripts — guard-yield.sh's likely-false-positive heuristic — can call:
+#
+#   heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   prints interpreter|nonexec|none
+#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>          exit 0 iff the command's heredocs
+#                                           all have non-executing consumers
+#
+# Source only; never execute. Bash 3.2 compatible. When the fence cannot be
+# read the functions report "none" / exit 1, which callers treat as "no
+# classifier" (guard-yield.sh falls back to `<<` presence).
+_hc_lib_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+_hc_fence="${_hc_lib_dir}/../../hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
+if [[ -r "$_hc_fence" ]]; then
+  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
+  BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 source "$_hc_fence"
+fi
+unset _hc_lib_dir _hc_fence
+
+heredoc_consumer_class() {
+  if declare -F _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}"
+  else
+    printf 'none\n'
+  fi
+}
+
+heredoc_nonexec() {
+  [[ "$(heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
+}

    10	#   loa_knob <yq-path> <fallback>   → the effective value of one config key:
    11	#        the key set explicitly in the config (an explicit `false` counts —
    12	#        never `// default`, which reads false as absent), else the selected
    13	#        profile's value when the key is a profile key, else <fallback>.
    14	#        Returns 2 (printing the fallback) on a malformed path.
    15	#   loa_profile_overrides           → `key=value` lines, one per explicit
    16	#        profile key whose value differs from the selected profile's value

    26	#   root      LOA_PROFILE_ROOT, else three directories above this file
    27	#

    29	# keyed on the paths and the mtime+size of the config, profiles.yaml and
    30	# floor.yaml: any edit to one of them rebuilds it on the next call, so it is
    31	# built once per session in practice. When the config is a seam (not the
    32	# repository's own file) and no cache seam is set, nothing is cached — a test
    33	# config never overwrites the repository's cache. The warm path is one stat
    34	# and one jq. The write is atomic (temp file + mv in the same directory).
    35	#

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# run-checkpoint.sh — run position in .run/ (cycle-125 FR-3, SDD D-3.2;
# cycle-129 FR-4(f)/FR-5, SDD D-4.6, D-5.1 … D-5.4). Beads are the task ledger;
# the checkpoint is a HINT; the run state and the breaker are caches DERIVED
# from files (COMPLETED markers, LOA-VERDICT trailers, the ledger, git).
#
#   run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint sprint-N --phase PHASE [--task BEAD-ID] [--file F]
#       Atomically sets .schema_version = 2, .checkpoint = {sprint, task, phase, ts}
#       and .timestamps.last_activity = ts: jq → F.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock
#       on F.lock. F must already exist (a run in progress). Then runs
#       `derive --write` (a missing ledger is skipped). Exit 0 · 2 usage /
#       no run · 3 write failed (the previous file is untouched).
#   run-checkpoint.sh read [--file F] [--json]
#       Prints the checkpoint when it is trustworthy: parses, and when a task
#       is named, `br show <task> --json` reports it closed (a checkpoint that
#       names an open or unknown bead is DISCARDED with a logged line — beads
#       remain the recovery source). schema_version 1 / no checkpoint → prints
#       "sprint granularity". Exit 0 always when F exists; 2 when it does not.
#   run-checkpoint.sh derive [--json] [--write] [--root DIR] [--file F]
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
VERDICT_DERIVE="$SCRIPT_DIR/verdict-derive.sh"
usage() { sed -n '3,/^# Default F/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }

sub="${1:-}"; [[ -n "$sub" ]] || usage; shift
file="" sprint="" task="" phase="" json=0 write=0 root="" gate="" state_file="" breaker="" skill=""
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --file)   [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --sprint) [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; sprint="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --task)   [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; task="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --phase)  [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Z_]+$ ]] || usage; phase="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --json)   json=1; shift ;;
    --write)  write=1; shift ;;
    --root)   [[ $# -ge 2 && -d "${2:-}" ]] || usage; root="$(cd "$2" && pwd)"; shift 2 ;;
    --gate)   [[ $# -ge 2 && ( "$2" == review || "$2" == audit ) ]] || usage; gate="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --state-file|--file-state) [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; state_file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --breaker) [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; breaker="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --skill)  [[ $# -ge 2 && ( "$2" == implement || "$2" == bug ) ]] || usage; skill="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    *) usage ;;
  esac
done

# Root and run dir: --root wins (and pins the run dir under it); else the
# directory holding a --file that sits in a .run/ dir (write/read/derive only);
# else this script's checkout with $LOA_RUN_DIR honoured.
if [[ -n "$root" ]]; then
  run_dir="$root/.run"
else
  root="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  run_dir="${LOA_RUN_DIR:-$root/.run}"
  if [[ -n "$file" && "$sub" != record-round ]]; then
    fdir="$(cd "$(dirname "$file")" 2>/dev/null && pwd)" || fdir=""
    if [[ -n "$fdir" && "$(basename "$fdir")" == .run ]]; then root="$(dirname "$fdir")"; run_dir="$fdir"; fi
  fi
fi
if [[ "$sub" != record-round && -z "$file" ]]; then file="$run_dir/sprint-plan-state.json"; fi
[[ -n "$breaker" ]] || breaker="$run_dir/circuit-breaker.json"
[[ -n "$state_file" ]] || state_file="$run_dir/state.json"
CONFIG="$root/.loa.config.yaml"

now_iso() { date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ; }

# cfg KEY → the raw yq value ("null" when absent or unreadable). yq's `//`
# treats false as absent, so callers compare the raw text.
cfg() {
  if (( drc != 0 && drc != 4 )); then printf '%s\n' "$err" >&2; fi
  return 0
}

bead_closed() {  # $1 bead id → 0 when br reports closed
  command -v br >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 2
  local js st
  js=$(br show "$1" --json 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  st=$(printf '%s' "$js" | jq -r 'if type=="array" then .[0] else . end | .status // .issue.status // empty' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  [[ "$st" == "closed" ]]
}

cmd_read() {
  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
  if ! jq -e . "$file" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "run-checkpoint: $file unparseable — no checkpoint; beads are the recovery truth" >&2; if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"unparseable"}'; fi; return 0; fi
  local sv cp s t p ts reason="" brc
  sv=$(jq -r '.schema_version // 1' "$file"); cp=$(jq -c '.checkpoint // null' "$file")
  [[ "$sv" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || sv=1
  if [[ "$cp" == "null" || "$sv" -lt 2 ]]; then
    if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"sprint granularity"}'; else echo "checkpoint: none (schema_version $sv → sprint granularity; resume at the first open bead of sprints.current)"; fi
    return 0
  fi
  s=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.sprint // empty' "$file"); t=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.task // empty' "$file"); p=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.phase // empty' "$file"); ts=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.ts // empty' "$file")
  if [[ -z "$s" || -z "$p" ]]; then reason="malformed checkpoint"
  elif [[ -n "$t" ]]; then
    # A task checkpoint is trusted only when beads CONFIRMS the task closed;
    # "br unavailable" is not a confirmation (Bridgebuilder PR #1269 FIND-003).
    brc=0; bead_closed "$t" || brc=$?
    case $brc in 0) ;; 2) reason="beads unavailable — task $t cannot be verified";; *) reason="task $t is not closed in beads";; esac
  fi
  if [[ -n "$reason" ]]; then
    echo "run-checkpoint: discarding checkpoint ($reason) — resume from the first open bead of $s" >&2
    if (( json )); then jq -cn --arg r "$reason" --arg s "$s" '{checkpoint:null, reason:$r, sprint:$s}'; else echo "checkpoint: discarded ($reason); resume at the first open bead of $s"; fi
    return 0
  fi
  if (( json )); then jq -c '{checkpoint: .checkpoint}' "$file"
  else echo "checkpoint: $s ${t:+task $t }phase $p at $ts → resume at the first open bead after $t in $s"; fi
}

# fb_parse FILE GATE → one compact JSON object: {file, exists, trailer, verdict,
# counts, exit_code, sprint_id, ts, approved, hash}. The hash is the run-mode

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tests/unit/profile-floor.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.7 (AC-2.9; PRD
     4	# AC-9.2; SDD D-9.2, DEC-0166)
     5	#
     6	# No profile can reach the floor. The floor source is .claude/data/floor.yaml
     7	# (read here, never duplicated); its sha256 pin is READ from
     8	# tests/unit/guard-origins.bats (FLOOR_SHA256) so the two suites cannot
     9	# disagree. Under `lean` every floor surface reads byte-identically to
    10	# `standard`: the floor config keys (the two gate skills' flatline_protocol.*
    11	# config, destructive_command_guard.*, implement_gate.*, hounfour.locality),
    12	# verdict-derive.sh on fixture feedback files, the adversarial gate's
    13	# decision and environment, the deny-list file, the fence on the corpus and
    14	# the FR-1.2b / FR-SZ probes, and user-invoked-commands.txt.
    15	# =============================================================================
    16	
    17	bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
    18	
    19	setup() {
    20	    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    21	    LIB="$R/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh"
    22	    PROFILES="$R/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
    23	    FLOOR="$R/.claude/data/floor.yaml"
    24	    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
    25	    # Two configs that differ ONLY in loa.profile: this repository's own config
    26	    # (which carries the floor keys it really uses) with the profile set.
    27	    for p in lean standard; do
    28	        cp "$R/.loa.config.yaml" "$T/$p.yaml"
    29	        yq -i ".loa.profile = \"$p\"" "$T/$p.yaml"
    30	    done
    31	    unset LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE LOA_PROFILES_FILE
    32	}
    33	
    34	# The floor key patterns, as the lib and the guard register read them.
    35	floor_keys() { yq -r '.floor_keys[]' "$FLOOR"; }
    36	
    37	@test "PF-1 floor.yaml matches the sha256 pin guard-origins.bats carries (one constant, two suites)" {
    38	    local pin actual
    39	    pin=$(sed -n 's/^FLOOR_SHA256="\([0-9a-f]\{64\}\)"$/\1/p' "$R/tests/unit/guard-origins.bats")
    40	    [ -n "$pin" ] || { echo "no FLOOR_SHA256 in guard-origins.bats"; return 1; }
    41	    actual=$(bash -c 'source "$1/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; sha256_portable "$2"' _ "$R" "$FLOOR" | cut -d' ' -f1)
    42	    [ "$actual" = "$pin" ] || { echo "floor.yaml sha256 $actual != pinned $pin"; return 1; }
    43	}
    44	
    45	@test "PF-2 no profiles.yaml key matches a floor key or is an ancestor of one" {
    46	    run python3 -I - "$PROFILES" "$FLOOR" <<'PY'
    47	import re, subprocess, sys, json
    48	def load(p):
    49	    return json.loads(subprocess.check_output(["yq", "-o=json", ".", p]))
    50	prof, floor = load(sys.argv[1]), load(sys.argv[2])
    51	keys = sorted({k for v in prof["profiles"].values() for k in v})
    52	assert len(keys) == 9, keys
    53	bad = []
    54	for k in keys:
    55	    for f in floor["floor_keys"]:
    56	        rx = "^" + ".+".join(re.escape(s) for s in f.split("*")) + "$"
    57	        if re.match(rx, k) or f.split("*")[0].startswith(k + "."):
    58	            bad.append((k, f))
    59	print("violations:", bad)
    60	sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
    61	PY
    62	    echo "$output"
    63	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    64	    # floor_keys_forbidden is not duplicated into profiles.yaml.
    65	    [ "$(yq -r 'has("floor_keys_forbidden")' "$PROFILES")" = "false" ]
    66	}
    67	
    68	@test "PF-3 under lean the resolved document names no floor key and every floor key reads as under standard" {
    69	    local p k
    70	    for p in lean standard; do
    71	        LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" bash "$LIB" json > "$T/$p.json"
    72	        [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$T/$p.json")" = "$p" ]
    73	    done
    74	    # Concrete floor keys: every leaf path of this config and the example that a
    75	    # floor pattern matches (flatline_protocol.*.companion_voice expands here).
    76	    yq -o=json '.' "$R/.loa.config.yaml" > "$T/cfg.json"
    77	    yq -o=json '.' "$R/.loa.config.yaml.example" > "$T/ex.json"
    78	    floor_keys > "$T/floor.txt"
    79	    python3 -I - "$T/cfg.json" "$T/ex.json" "$T/floor.txt" > "$T/concrete.txt" <<'PY'
    80	import json, re, sys
    81	pats = [l.strip() for l in open(sys.argv[3]) if l.strip()]
    82	rxs = ["^" + ".+".join(re.escape(s) for s in p.split("*")) + "$" for p in pats]
    83	out = set(p for p in pats if "*" not in p)
    84	def walk(x, path):
    85	    if isinstance(x, dict):
    86	        for k, v in x.items():
    87	            walk(v, path + [str(k)])
    88	    if path:
    89	        key = ".".join(path)
    90	        if any(re.match(r, key) for r in rxs):
    91	            out.add(key)

   101	        a=$(LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/lean.yaml" bash "$LIB" knob "$k" __unset__ 2>/dev/null)
   102	        b=$(LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/standard.yaml" bash "$LIB" knob "$k" __unset__ 2>/dev/null)
   103	        [ "$a" = "$b" ] || { echo "$k: lean=$a standard=$b"; return 1; }
   104	    done < "$T/concrete.txt"
   105	    # The two gate skills' whole flatline_protocol config is byte-identical.
   106	    for g in code_review security_audit; do

   111	@test "PF-4 verdict-derive.sh output is byte-identical under lean and standard" {

   128	@test "PF-5 the adversarial-review gate decides identically under lean and standard" {

   137	        echo "$rc" >> "$T/gate-$p.out"

   142	    # The gate's environment knob is not a profile key and the gate never sources the lib.
   143	    ! grep -q 'profile-lib' "$R/.claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# profile-lib.sh — `loa.profile` resolution (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §5.3;
# DEC-0143, DEC-0152, DEC-0166).
#
# Sourced API (bash 3.2 safe; sets no shell options; every function returns 0
# unless stated):
#   loa_profile                     → lean | standard | full
#   loa_profile_source              → explicit | default | invalid
#   loa_knob <yq-path> <fallback>   → the effective value of one config key:
#        the key set explicitly in the config (an explicit `false` counts —
#        never `// default`, which reads false as absent), else the selected
#        profile's value when the key is a profile key, else <fallback>.
#        Returns 2 (printing the fallback) on a malformed path.
#   loa_profile_overrides           → `key=value` lines, one per explicit
#        profile key whose value differs from the selected profile's value
#   loa_effective_json              → the resolved document (below)
#
# CLI: profile-lib.sh profile | source | knob <path> <fallback> | overrides | json
#
# Inputs (each has a test seam):
#   config    LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE, else LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE (honoured
#             only under bats, like loa-status.sh), else <root>/.loa.config.yaml
#   profiles  LOA_PROFILES_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/profiles.yaml
#   floor     LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/floor.yaml
#   root      LOA_PROFILE_ROOT, else three directories above this file
#
# Cache: <root>/.run/effective-config.json (LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE overrides),
# keyed on the paths and the mtime+size of the config, profiles.yaml and
# floor.yaml: any edit to one of them rebuilds it on the next call, so it is
# built once per session in practice. When the config is a seam (not the
# repository's own file) and no cache seam is set, nothing is cached — a test
# config never overwrites the repository's cache. The warm path is one stat
# and one jq. The write is atomic (temp file + mv in the same directory).
#
# Safety: a profile key that names a floor key (floor.yaml `floor_keys`, `*`
# matches one or more characters; an ancestor of a floor key also counts) is
# ignored with a WARN — no profile can reach the floor. Key paths are checked
# against ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ before they reach a yq expression.
# Overrides and the requested profile name are control-stripped and cut.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# loa-kf-surface.sh — SessionStart hook (cycle-115 sprint-1, D1).
     4	#
     5	# Surfaces a compact symptom -> KF table from grimoires/loa/known-failures.md
     6	# at session start so an agent sees the operational-failure log before
     7	# triaging. DEFAULT-OFF: gated on `known_failures.surface_at_session_start`
     8	# (default false) in .loa.config.yaml.
     9	#
    10	# STREAM ROUTING: Claude Code's SessionStart contract injects a hook's STDOUT
    11	#   (on exit 0) into the session as context; STDERR is transcript-only and never
    12	#   reaches the agent. This surface is only useful IN CONTEXT, so every ENABLED
    13	#   path — the healthy table AND the enabled-but-degraded WARNINGs — writes to
    14	#   STDOUT (an agent under the index-first intake contract must SEE that the KF
    15	#   surface is degraded so it falls back to regenerating the index). Sibling
    16	#   surfacing hooks (loa-l6-surface-handoffs.sh, loa-l7-surface-soul.sh) route
    17	#   the same way. The DISABLED path emits nothing at all.
    18	#
    19	# CONTRACT (loud-but-nonblocking — this is OBSERVABILITY, never a gate):
    20	#   - It MUST exit 0 in ALL paths. It MUST NOT block a session.
    21	#   - When the flag is DISABLED (or config/yq absent): emit NOTHING, exit 0.
    22	#   - When ENABLED but the surface is degraded — known-failures.md unreadable,
    23	#     or zero KF entries parsed — emit a visible "[KF-SURFACE] WARNING ..."
    24	#     to STDOUT and exit 0 (loud + in-context, so the agent notices a broken
    25	#     knowledge surface; never silent on an enabled-but-broken path).
    26	#   - When ENABLED and healthy: emit a compact symptom -> KF table to STDOUT,
    27	#     exit 0.
    28	#
    29	# TRUST BOUNDARY: known-failures.md bodies are UNTRUSTED at surfacing. Every
    30	#   field is control-byte-sanitized + length-capped before reaching session
    31	#   context; body prose is NEVER interpreted as instructions (CLAUDE.md
    32	#   agent-network universal invariant).
    33	# =============================================================================
    34	set -uo pipefail
    35	
    36	HOOK_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    37	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${HOOK_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"
    38	
    39	# --- test-mode seam (mirrors L4/L6/L7 cycle-098 gate): the config + path
    40	#     overrides are honored ONLY under LOA_KF_SURFACE_TEST_MODE=1 with a bats
    41	#     marker present. In production neither override is consulted. -----------
    42	_kf_test_mode_active() {
    43	  [[ "${LOA_KF_SURFACE_TEST_MODE:-0}" == "1" ]] || return 1
    44	  [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}" ]] && return 0
    45	  [[ -n "${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]] && return 0
    46	  return 1
    47	}
    48	
    49	# Sanitize: drop control bytes (keep UTF-8 multibyte), flatten whitespace, cap.
    50	_san() { printf '%s' "${1-}" | tr -d '\000-\010\013\014\016-\037\177' | tr '\t\n\r' '   ' | sed -E 's/  +/ /g; s/^ //; s/ $//' | cut -c1-100; }
    51	
    52	# --- resolve enabled flag -----------------------------------------------------
    53	enabled="false"
    54	if _kf_test_mode_active && [[ -n "${LOA_KF_SURFACE_TEST_CONFIG-}" ]]; then
    55	  # In test mode the override stands in for the parsed config value.
    56	  enabled="${LOA_KF_SURFACE_TEST_CONFIG}"
    57	else
    58	  config_path="${REPO_ROOT}/.loa.config.yaml"
    59	  # No yq or no config -> the feature is opt-in and unconfigurable here: silent.
    60	  if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f "$config_path" ]]; then
    61	    # Explicit key, else the loa.profile default (cycle-129 D-9.1).
    62	    # shellcheck source=scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
    63	    source "${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null &&
    64	      enabled="$(loa_knob known_failures.surface_at_session_start false 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
    65	  fi
    66	fi
    67	
    68	# DISABLED (or unconfigurable) -> emit nothing, exit 0. This is the ONLY silent path.
    69	[[ "$enabled" == "true" ]] || exit 0
    70	
    71	# --- ENABLED: from here every exit is loud-or-table, always exit 0 -----------
    72	KF_FILE="${REPO_ROOT}/grimoires/loa/known-failures.md"
    73	if _kf_test_mode_active && [[ -n "${LOA_KNOWN_FAILURES_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    74	  KF_FILE="${LOA_KNOWN_FAILURES_FILE}"
    75	fi
    76	
    77	if [[ ! -r "$KF_FILE" ]]; then
    78	  echo "[KF-SURFACE] WARNING: known-failures.md is unreadable at ${KF_FILE} — the known-failures surface is enabled but degraded. Triage without it; check the file path."
    79	  exit 0
    80	fi
    81	
    82	# Parse id + symptom from each ## KF-NNN: entry (source of truth), deduped by
    83	# id. Mirrors grimoire-index.sh emit_kf field-parsing (both field variants).
    84	# Output is TAB-delimited: id<TAB>recurrence<TAB>symptom.
    85	rows="$(awk '
    86	  function fieldval(line, label,   reA, reB, v) {
    87	    reA = "^(- )?\\*\\*" label "\\*\\*: ?"
    88	    reB = "^(- )?\\*\\*" label "[^*]*:\\*\\* ?"
    89	    if (line ~ reA) { v = line; sub(reA, "", v); return v }
    90	    if (line ~ reB) { v = line; sub(reB, "", v); return v }
    91	    return ""
    92	  }
    93	  /^## KF-[0-9]+:/ {
    94	    if (match($0, /KF-[0-9]+/)) { id = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH) } else { id = "" }
    95	    if (id != "" && !(id in seen)) { order[++n] = id; seen[id] = 1 }
    96	    cur = id; next
    97	  }
    98	  cur != "" {
    99	    if (sy[cur] == "") { v = fieldval($0, "Symptom");          if (v != "") { sy[cur] = v; next } }
   100	    if (rc[cur] == "") { v = fieldval($0, "Recurrence count"); if (v != "") { rc[cur] = v; next } }
   101	  }
   102	  END {
   103	    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
   104	      id = order[i]; r = rc[id]; num = "?"; v = r
   105	      gsub(/^([>=~ ]|\342\211\245)+/, "", v)
   106	      if (match(v, /^[0-9]+/)) num = substr(v, RSTART, RLENGTH)
   107	      printf "%s\t%s\t%s\n", id, num, sy[id]
   108	    }
   109	  }
   110	' "$KF_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"

     3	# block-destructive-bash hook and summarise (cycle-125 Sprint 1, PRD FR-1).
     4	#
     5	# Usage: run-corpus.sh [--hook PATH] [--corpus PATH] [--json] [--knob-off] [--rows]
     6	# Each row: {id, cmd, expect: allow|block|residual, rule, why, cwd: repo|tmp, env?: {TMPDIR}}
     7	#   allow    → benign: the hook must exit 0
     8	#   block    → dangerous: the hook must exit 2
     9	#   residual → accepted false positive: counted, never gated
    10	# --knob-off  writes destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier: false into the
    11	#             replay root's .loa.config.yaml (cycle-129 FR-6: the pre-cycle scan);
    12	#             compare it with the pre-change hook through --rows.
    13	# --rows      prints "<id> <exit code>" per row instead of the summary (for diffs).
    14	# Output (text): one line per mismatch, then
    15	#   "benign P/T dangerous B/T residual R/T runtime_ms N p95_ms M";
    16	# --json prints {benign_pass, benign_total, dangerous_block, dangerous_total,
    17	#   residual_pass, residual_total, runtime_ms, p95_ms, rows, mismatches: [..]}.
    18	# p95_ms is the 95th percentile of the per-row hook wall time (the hook process
    19	# only; the jq row parsing is outside the timed span).
    20	set -uo pipefail
    21	export LC_ALL=C
    22	root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../.." && pwd)"
    23	hook="$root/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
    24	corpus="$root/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl"
    25	json=0 knob_off=0 rows_out=0
    26	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    27	  case "$1" in
    28	    --hook) hook="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    29	    --corpus) corpus="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    30	    --json) json=1; shift ;;
    31	    --knob-off) knob_off=1; shift ;;
    32	    --rows) rows_out=1; shift ;;
    33	    *) echo "usage: run-corpus.sh [--hook PATH] [--corpus PATH] [--json] [--knob-off] [--rows]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    34	  esac
    35	done
    36	[[ -x "$hook" || -f "$hook" ]] || { echo "hook not found: $hook" >&2; exit 2; }
    37	[[ -f "$corpus" ]] || { echo "corpus not found: $corpus" >&2; exit 2; }
    38	
    39	work="$(mktemp -d)"
    40	trap 'rm -rf -- "$work"' EXIT
    41	repo="$work/repo"; scratch="$work/scratch"
    42	mkdir -p "$repo" "$scratch"
    43	export LOA_REPO_ROOT="$work"
    44	export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1   # audit rows this replay writes carry replay: true (cycle-129 DEC-0167)
    45	if (( knob_off )); then
    46	  printf 'destructive_command_guard:\n  heredoc_classifier: false\n' > "$work/.loa.config.yaml"
    47	fi
    48	
    49	bp=0 bt=0 db=0 dt=0 rp=0 rt=0
    50	mismatches=()
    51	durations=()
    52	# Microsecond clock: $EPOCHREALTIME (bash ≥ 5) everywhere; GNU date fallback.
    53	now_us() {
    54	  if [[ -n "${EPOCHREALTIME:-}" ]]; then
    55	    local s="${EPOCHREALTIME%.*}" us="${EPOCHREALTIME#*.}"
    56	    echo $(( s * 1000000 + 10#${us:0:6} ))
    57	  else
    58	    echo $(( $(date +%s%N) / 1000 ))
    59	  fi
    60	}
    61	start_us=$(now_us)
    62	while IFS= read -r row; do
    63	  [[ -n "$row" ]] || continue
    64	  id=$(jq -r '.id' <<<"$row"); cmd=$(jq -r '.cmd' <<<"$row"); expect=$(jq -r '.expect' <<<"$row")
    65	  cwd=$(jq -r '.cwd // "repo"' <<<"$row"); tmpdir=$(jq -r '.env.TMPDIR // empty' <<<"$row")
    66	  dir="$repo"; [[ "$cwd" == "tmp" ]] && dir="$scratch"
    67	  payload=$(jq -cn --arg c "$cmd" '{tool_input: {command: $c}}')
    68	  rc=0
    69	  t0=$(now_us)
    70	  if [[ -n "$tmpdir" ]]; then
    71	    (cd "$dir" && TMPDIR="$tmpdir" bash "$hook" <<<"$payload" >/dev/null 2>&1) || rc=$?
    72	  else
    73	    (cd "$dir" && env -u TMPDIR bash "$hook" <<<"$payload" >/dev/null 2>&1) || rc=$?
    74	  fi
    75	  t1=$(now_us)
    76	  durations+=("$(( (t1 - t0) / 1000 ))")
    77	  (( rows_out )) && printf '%s %s\n' "$id" "$rc"
    78	  case "$expect" in
    79	    allow)    bt=$((bt+1)); if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then bp=$((bp+1)); else mismatches+=("$id:expected-allow:rc=$rc"); fi ;;
    80	    block)    dt=$((dt+1)); if [[ $rc -eq 2 ]]; then db=$((db+1)); else mismatches+=("$id:expected-block:rc=$rc"); fi ;;
    81	    residual) rt=$((rt+1)); [[ $rc -eq 0 ]] && rp=$((rp+1)) ;;
    82	    *) mismatches+=("$id:unknown-expect:$expect") ;;
    83	  esac
    84	done < "$corpus"
    85	end_us=$(now_us)
    86	runtime=$(( (end_us - start_us) / 1000 ))
    87	n=${#durations[@]}
    88	p95=0
    89	if (( n > 0 )); then
    90	  idx=$(( (n * 95 + 99) / 100 ))      # nearest-rank: ceil(0.95 n)
    91	  p95=$(printf '%s\n' "${durations[@]}" | sort -n | sed -n "${idx}p")
    92	fi
    93	
    94	(( rows_out )) && exit 0
    95	if (( json )); then
    96	  printf '%s\n' "${mismatches[@]+"${mismatches[@]}"}" | jq -R . | jq -s \
    97	    --argjson bp "$bp" --argjson bt "$bt" --argjson db "$db" --argjson dt "$dt" \
    98	    --argjson rp "$rp" --argjson rt "$rt" --argjson ms "$runtime" --argjson p95 "$p95" --argjson n "$n" \
    99	    '{benign_pass:$bp, benign_total:$bt, dangerous_block:$db, dangerous_total:$dt, residual_pass:$rp, residual_total:$rt, runtime_ms:$ms, p95_ms:$p95, rows:$n, mismatches: map(select(length>0))}'
   100	else
   101	  printf '%s\n' "${mismatches[@]+"${mismatches[@]}"}" | sed '/^$/d'
   102	  echo "benign $bp/$bt dangerous $db/$dt residual $rp/$rt runtime_ms $runtime p95_ms $p95"
   103	fi

# Input Guardrails & Danger Level Enforcement (v1.20.0)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pre-execution validation for skill invocations. Provides PII filtering,
# injection detection, and relevance checking before skills execute.
# Based on OpenAI's "A Practical Guide to Building Agents" guardrails pattern.
guardrails:
  # Input guardrails (pre-execution)
  input:
    enabled: true

    # PII Filter: Detect and redact sensitive data before processing
    # Actions: redact (replace with placeholder), anonymize (generic value)
    pii_filter:
      enabled: true
      mode: blocking              # blocking | parallel | advisory
      patterns:
        api_keys: true            # sk-*, ghp_*, AKIA*
        emails: true              # user@example.com
        phone_numbers: true       # 555-123-4567
        ssn: true                 # 123-45-6789
        credit_cards: true        # 4111-1111-1111-1111
        jwt_tokens: true          # eyJ... tokens
        private_keys: true        # -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----
        file_paths: anonymize     # anonymize | redact | ignore
      log_redactions: true        # Log redaction count (never values)

3:--- a/.loa.config.yaml.example
4:+++ b/.loa.config.yaml.example
9:+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
10:+# Profile (cycle-129, DEC-0143)
11:+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
12:+# One knob sets the defaults of the optional surfaces as a set:
13:+#   known_failures.surface_at_session_start, decisions.surface_at_session_start,
14:+#   karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning,
15:+#   karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria, guardrails.input.enabled,
16:+#   guardrails.danger_level.enforce, invisible_retrospective.enabled,
17:+#   structured_handoff.enabled, soul_identity_doc.enabled
18:+# `lean` turns them all off, `full` all on, and `standard` (the default) is the
19:+# per-key default this file shows (soul_identity_doc.enabled, not shown here,
20:+# is false). A key you set explicitly anywhere in
21:+# this file wins over the profile. The values per profile live in
22:+# .claude/data/profiles.yaml; `/loa` prints the effective profile and your
23:+# explicit overrides. No floor key is reachable through a profile: review,
24:+# audit, verdict-derive, the dissent artefact gate, the deny list, the
25:+# destructive-command fence, the System-Zone rules and every other floor
26:+# config key read the same configuration under every profile
27:+# (.claude/data/floor.yaml lists them; tests/unit/profile-floor.bats pins it).
28:+# An unknown value warns and falls back to standard.
29:+loa:
30:+  profile: standard   # lean | standard | full
31:+
39:+  # Run position from files (cycle-129 FR-5): `run-checkpoint.sh derive` rebuilds
40:+  # .run/sprint-plan-state.json (.state canonical, .status mirrored, derived_at) and
41:+  # .run/circuit-breaker.json from COMPLETED markers, LOA-VERDICT trailers, the ledger
42:+  # and git at every checkpoint. false = report-only (the caches are written as before;
43:+  # the rollback key).
44:+  file_authoritative: true
45:+  # Hours after which a RUNNING run with no activity derives to INTERRUPTED, and after
46:+  # which a derived cache (derived_at) no longer counts as a known run position for the
47:+  # implement gate. Positive integer.
48:+  stale_hours: 12
56:+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
57:+# Implement gate (cycle-129 FR-4(a); hook: .claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh)
58:+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
59:+# PreToolUse check on Write/Edit/NotebookEdit into the App Zone (src/, lib/, app/)
60:+# outside an implementation run. A write is SANCTIONED (allowed, one audit row each) by:
61:+#   - a RUNNING run cache (.run/sprint-plan-state.json or .run/state.json, fresh
62:+#     last_activity, and derived_at within run_mode.stale_hours when present);
63:+#   - .run/implement-active.json {skill: implement|bug, sprint, started_at} younger than
64:+#     two hours (`run-checkpoint.sh mark` at the start of /implement and /bug, `unmark`
65:+#     at the end); a stale or malformed marker is logged and does not sanction;
66:+#   - LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE=1 in the session environment (audited, one row per write).
67:+# An unsanctioned App-Zone write is then handled by `mode`:
68:+#   ask        (default) asks for confirmation, as before, and logs one row per ask
69:+#   telemetry  logs one row to .run/audit.jsonl and allows silently
70:+#   deny       refuses the write when the derived run position is known (the cache parses
71:+#              and its derived_at is within run_mode.stale_hours); an unknown position
72:+#              (missing, not derived, stale, unparseable) asks instead, never allows.
73:+#              The hook is a fence only in this mode.
74:+# Writes to the gate's own inputs (.run state files, .run/audit.jsonl, the marker,
75:+# .loa.config.yaml) ask in every mode and under every sanction.
76:+# `claims: authoritative` is a tighten-only modifier for any mode: a model-authored
77:+# tool_input.active_skill naming a non-implementation skill asks (or, under deny, is
78:+# denied), and never allows by itself. The legacy `mode: authoritative` means
79:+# mode: ask + claims: authoritative. /loa prints the effective mode on its Gate line.
80:+implement_gate:
81:+  mode: ask                      # ask | telemetry | deny
82:+  # claims: authoritative        # optional, tighten-only
83:+
91:+  # Heredoc consumer classifier (cycle-129 FR-6). true (default): the Bash
92:+  # fence scans a heredoc body in full only when its consumer may execute it,
93:+  # and scans a non-executing body per segment. false: the pre-cycle scan
94:+  # (rollback key; turning it off only tightens). See hooks-reference.md,
95:+  # "Heredoc consumer classification".
96:+  heredoc_classifier: true
97:+
105:+#
106:+# Default OFF since cycle-129 (DEC-0161): across 82 recorded guardrail events
107:+# the input guardrails caught nothing, and danger-level enforcement blocked
108:+# the sanctioned skills seven times. Turn them on with
109:+# `guardrails.input.enabled: true` (the orchestrator then logs PASS/BLOCK
110:+# events to the trajectory) and `guardrails.danger_level.enforce: true`.
111:+# Both keys are part of the `loa.profile` set (`full` turns them on).
115:-    enabled: true
116:+    enabled: false
124:-    enforce: true
