#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# profile-lib.sh — `loa.profile` resolution (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §5.3;
# DEC-0143, DEC-0152, DEC-0166).
#
# Sourced API (bash 3.2 safe; sets no shell options; every function returns 0
# unless stated):
#   loa_profile                     → lean | standard | full
#   loa_profile_source              → explicit | default | invalid
#   loa_knob <yq-path> <fallback>   → the effective value of one config key:
#        the key set explicitly in the config (an explicit `false` counts —
#        never `// default`, which reads false as absent), else the selected
#        profile's value when the key is a profile key, else <fallback>.
#        Returns 2 (printing the fallback) on a malformed path.
#   loa_profile_overrides           → `key=value` lines, one per explicit
#        profile key whose value differs from the selected profile's value
#   loa_effective_json              → the resolved document (below)
#
# CLI: profile-lib.sh profile | source | knob <path> <fallback> | overrides | json
#
# Inputs (each has a test seam):
#   config    LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE, else LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE (honoured
#             only under bats, like loa-status.sh), else <root>/.loa.config.yaml
#   profiles  LOA_PROFILES_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/profiles.yaml
#   floor     LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/floor.yaml
#   root      LOA_PROFILE_ROOT, else three directories above this file
#
# Cache: <root>/.run/effective-config.json (LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE overrides),
# keyed on the paths and the mtime+size of the config, profiles.yaml and
# floor.yaml: any edit to one of them rebuilds it on the next call, so it is
# built once per session in practice. When the config is a seam (not the
# repository's own file) and no cache seam is set, nothing is cached — a test
# config never overwrites the repository's cache. The warm path is one stat
# and one jq. The write is atomic (temp file + mv in the same directory).
#
# Safety: a profile key that names a floor key (floor.yaml `floor_keys`, `*`
# matches one or more characters; an ancestor of a floor key also counts) is
# ignored with a WARN — no profile can reach the floor. Key paths are checked
# against ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ before they reach a yq expression.
# Overrides and the requested profile name are control-stripped and cut.
# =============================================================================

_LOA_PL_SELF="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="${_LOA_PL_SELF%/*}"
[[ "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" == "$_LOA_PL_SELF" ]] && _LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="."
_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
_LOA_PL_JSON=""
_LOA_PL_ID=""

_loa_pl_paths() {
  local root="${LOA_PROFILE_ROOT:-}"
  if [[ -z "$root" ]]; then
    root="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
  fi
  _LOA_PL_ROOT="$root"
  local default_cfg="$root/.loa.config.yaml" status_cfg=""
  # LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE is loa-status.sh's bats-gated seam; honour it the same way.
  if [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    status_cfg="${LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE:-}"
  fi
  _LOA_PL_CFG="${LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE:-${status_cfg:-$default_cfg}}"
  _LOA_PL_PROF="${LOA_PROFILES_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/profiles.yaml}"
  _LOA_PL_FLOOR="${LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/floor.yaml}"
  if [[ -n "${LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
  elif [[ "$_LOA_PL_CFG" == "$default_cfg" ]]; then
    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$root/.run/effective-config.json"
  else
    _LOA_PL_CACHE=""
  fi
}

# The cache key: the three paths plus one stat line per existing file. An
# empty stat output for an existing file (no usable stat) disables caching.
_loa_pl_id() {
  local st
  st=$(stat -Lc '%n|%y|%s' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) ||
    st=$(stat -Lf '%N|%Fm|%z' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || true
  if [[ -z "$st" ]] && [[ -e "$_LOA_PL_CFG" || -e "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
    _LOA_PL_CUR_ID=""
    return 0
  fi
  _LOA_PL_CUR_ID="v1|$_LOA_PL_CFG|$_LOA_PL_PROF|$_LOA_PL_FLOOR|${st//$'\n'/;}"
}

_loa_pl_warn() { printf '[profile-lib] WARN: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

# Builds the resolved document from the three inputs into _LOA_PL_JSON.
_loa_pl_build() {
  local cfg='{}' prof='{}' floor='[]' out
  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
    return 1
  fi
  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_CFG" ]]; then
    if ! cfg=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null); then
      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_CFG does not parse; profile defaults apply"
      cfg='{}'
    fi
  fi
  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
    if ! prof=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_PROF" 2>/dev/null); then
      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF does not parse; no profile defaults apply"
      prof='{}'
    fi
  else
    _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF is missing; no profile defaults apply"
  fi
  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" ]]; then
    floor=$(yq -o=json '.floor_keys // []' "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || floor='[]'
  fi
  [[ -n "$cfg" ]] || cfg='{}'
  [[ -n "$prof" ]] || prof='{}'
  [[ -n "$floor" ]] || floor='[]'
  out=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$cfg" "$prof" "$floor" | jq -cs --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" '
    def render: if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end;
    def clean($n): render | gsub("[[:cntrl:]]"; "?") | .[0:$n];
    def globre: "^" + (split("*") | map(gsub("\\."; "\\.")) | join(".+")) + "$";
    (.[0] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $cfg |
    (.[1] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pf |
  _LOA_PL_ID="$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID"
  _loa_pl_write_cache
  return 0
}

# Live read of one explicit key (non-profile keys, or no resolution available).
_loa_pl_live() {
  local key="$1" fallback="$2" v
  if [[ -f "${_LOA_PL_CFG:-}" ]] && command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    v=$(yq -o=json ".$key" "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'if . == null then "__LOA_PL_MISS__" elif type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end' 2>/dev/null) || v=""
    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$v"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
  return 0
}

loa_knob() {
  local path="${1:-}" fallback="${2:-}" key v
  key="${path#.}"
  if [[ ! "$key" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ ]]; then
    _loa_pl_warn "loa_knob: malformed key path '${path//[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/?}'"
    printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
    return 2
  fi
  # Warm path: one stat + one jq straight from the cache file.
  _loa_pl_paths
  _loa_pl_id
  if [[ -z "$_LOA_PL_JSON" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -f "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]] &&
     command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    v=$(jq -r --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" --arg k "$key" '
          if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then
            (if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
               | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
             else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end)
          else "__LOA_PL_STALE__" end' "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_STALE__"
    if [[ "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
      _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
      return 0
    fi
    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_STALE__" ]]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$v"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  if ! _loa_pl_load; then
    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
    return 0
  fi
  v=$(printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r --arg k "$key" '
        if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
          | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
        else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end' 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_MISS__"
  if [[ -z "$v" || "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
    return 0
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$v"
  return 0
}

loa_profile() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile // "standard"' 2>/dev/null || echo standard
  else
    echo standard
  fi
  return 0
}

loa_profile_source() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile_source // "default"' 2>/dev/null || echo default
  else
    echo default
  fi
  return 0
}

loa_profile_overrides() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.overrides[]?' 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  return 0
}

loa_effective_json() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s\n' "$_LOA_PL_JSON"
  else
    echo '{}'
  fi
  return 0
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
  export LC_ALL=C
  case "${1:-}" in
    profile)   loa_profile ;;
    source)    loa_profile_source ;;
    knob)      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "usage: profile-lib.sh knob <yq-path> [fallback]" >&2; exit 2; }
               loa_knob "$2" "${3:-}"; exit $? ;;
    overrides) loa_profile_overrides ;;
    json)      loa_effective_json ;;
    *)         sed -n '3,/^# =====/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
fi

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# heredoc-classifier.sh — library entry points for the FR-6 heredoc consumer
+# classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1). The single implementation lives in the fence,
+# .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh; this file sources it in
+# library mode (BDB_LIB_ONLY=1, which the fence honours only when sourced) so
+# other scripts — guard-yield.sh's likely-false-positive heuristic — can call:
+#
+#   heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   prints interpreter|nonexec|none
+#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>          exit 0 iff the command's heredocs
+#                                           all have non-executing consumers
+#
+# Source only; never execute. Bash 3.2 compatible. When the fence cannot be
+# read the functions report "none" / exit 1, which callers treat as "no
+# classifier" (guard-yield.sh falls back to `<<` presence).
+_hc_lib_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+_hc_fence="${_hc_lib_dir}/../../hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
+if [[ -r "$_hc_fence" ]]; then
+  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
+  BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 source "$_hc_fence"
+fi
+unset _hc_lib_dir _hc_fence
+
+heredoc_consumer_class() {
+  if declare -F _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}"
+  else
+    printf 'none\n'
+  fi
+}

+heredoc_nonexec() {

88:+Knob: `destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier` (default `true`; `false` restores the pre-cycle scan and is the rollback key). The fence reads the knob from `.loa.config.yaml` only for commands that hold `<<`. The full grammar, both class lists and the default are stated in the block comment above `_bdb_hd_is_interp` in `block-destructive-bash.sh`. In summary:
89-+
90:+- **Grammar.** The fence sees literal command text, with CRLF folded to LF. A control character, an unreadable header, more than one heredoc on a header, a non-word or variable delimiter, or a missing terminator makes the whole command scan in full.
91-+- **Interpreter class.** The body is scanned exactly as before. This applies when the consumer or any pipe target is a shell, interpreter, argument-running wrapper or SQL runner, when the statement holds a substitution, group or continuation, or when an allowlisted form carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag. It also applies when the write target is executable content: a script extension, a shebang first line, `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/settings*.json`, `.git/hooks/`, an rc or profile file, `/etc`, or a directory on `PATH`. Naming the target elsewhere on the same command outside a safe reader has the same effect.
92-+- **Non-executing class.** This covers exact forms only: `cat`, `tee`, `printf` and `echo` to a plain file or stdout, `gh pr|issue comment -F -`, `gh pr create --body-file -`, `git commit -F -`, `br create|update` reading stdin, `jq`/`yq` without in-place, `grep`, print-only `sed -n`, `sort` and `wc`. Their bodies are scanned per segment. Segments that start with a fence verb are kept for the normal rules, and the rest are dropped. A substitution under an unquoted delimiter, an interpreter word or a variable command word sends the body back to a full scan.
93-+- **Default.** A consumer on neither list, or a parse failure, scans in full. The #1245 quoted standalone `cat` scrub is the special case and is also the knob-off path.
94:+- **Export.** Source the hook with `BDB_LIB_ONLY=1` and call `_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command>`, which prints `interpreter`, `nonexec` or `none`. `heredoc_nonexec <command>` exits 0 for a non-executing heredoc. Library mode applies only when the file is sourced. An executed hook ignores the variable.
95-+- **Remaining gap.** A body written to a plain file by one command and executed by a later command is outside a per-command fence. The Write tool shares this limit.
96-+
97- **Accepted false positives (quote-blindness residue, cycle-120 C-D3)**: the inert-carrier scrub redacts a known data carrier's value (git commit `-m`, `br`/`bd -d`, `gh … create --body/--title`, `echo`/`printf`) only when the value holds **neither `$(` nor a backtick**. A lone `$` (dollar amount, `$ENV` mention, trailing bare `$`) is now permitted inside a redacted value — so `git commit -m "saved $5 by dropping find . -exec rm -rf {} +"` correctly ALLOWs. One residual false positive is **accepted by design**:
98- 
99- - **Case A — a `$(…)` command-substitution inside a carrier value** (e.g. a multi-line commit body wrapped in `$(cat <<'EOF' … find -exec rm -rf … EOF)`). The `$(` disqualifies the value from redaction (a regex fence cannot parse subshell contents without reintroducing the #1047 bypass), so a destructive *shape* mentioned inside that subshell body still trips FR-2 and blocks a genuinely safe commit. **Workaround**: paraphrase the destructive shape in the commit body (as the cycle-119 commits did — e.g. write "find-exec-rm" rather than the literal `find … -exec rm -rf`), or drop the `$(…)` wrapper. This is a preserved false positive, never a bypass: leaving `$(`/backtick values un-redacted is what keeps command-substitution smuggling (`git commit -m "$(rm -rf /)"`) caught. Backtick command-substitution itself remains the separately-tracked, uncaught pre-existing gap (bd-bdb-backtick-bypass).

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/profile-lib.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.7 (AC-2.9; PRD
# AC-9.1, AC-9.3; SDD D-9.1, D-9.3)
#
# .claude/data/profiles.yaml + .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh: precedence
# (explicit key > profile > fallback), every profile defines every key,
# `standard` equals the oracle captured before any reader changed
# (tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json), unknown profile, the
# mtime-keyed cache, the overrides line, the /loa Profile line, the readers
# that route through loa_knob, and the grep lint for direct reads.
# =============================================================================

bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0

setup() {
    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    LIB="$R/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh"
    PROFILES="$R/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
    ORACLE="$R/tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json"
    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
    CFG="$T/config.yaml"
    export LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$CFG"
    export LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE="$T/run/effective-config.json"
    : > "$CFG"
}

knob() { bash "$LIB" knob "$@"; }

@test "PL-1 every profile defines every key, and the key set is the nine optional keys" {
    run diff <(yq -r '.profiles.lean | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort) <(jq -r '.keys | keys[]' "$ORACLE" | sort)
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    for p in standard full; do
        run diff <(yq -r ".profiles.$p | keys | .[]" "$PROFILES" | sort) <(yq -r '.profiles.lean | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort)
        [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    done
    [ "$(yq -r '.profiles | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort | paste -sd, -)" = "full,lean,standard" ]
    [ "$(yq -r '.schema_version' "$PROFILES")" = "1" ]
    ! yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | grep -qx 'interview.pacing'
}

@test "PL-2 every profile value is a boolean; lean is all false and full all true" {
    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles[][] | tag] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "!!bool" ]
    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles.lean[]] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "false" ]
    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles.full[]] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "true" ]
}

@test "PL-3 standard equals the oracle captured before any reader changed" {
    local k want got
    while IFS= read -r k; do
        want=$(jq -r --arg k "$k" '.keys[$k].standard' "$ORACLE")
        got=$(yq -r ".profiles.standard[\"$k\"]" "$PROFILES")
        [ "$want" = "$got" ] || { echo "standard $k = $got, oracle $want"; return 1; }
    done < <(jq -r '.keys | keys[]' "$ORACLE")
    # Outside the two guardrail keys (whose default this cycle changes) the
    # oracle's standard IS the value the readers returned for the shipped example.
    run jq -r '.keys | to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith("guardrails.") | not)
               | select(.value.standard != .value.example_today) | .key' "$ORACLE"
    [ -z "$output" ]
    run jq -r '.keys | to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith("guardrails.")) | "\(.value.example_today)/\(.value.standard)"' "$ORACLE"
    [ "$(knob .guardrails.input.enabled true)" = "false" ]                   # leading dot accepted
}

@test "PL-7 an unknown profile warns once on stderr and resolves standard" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: turbo\n' > "$CFG"
    run --separate-stderr bash "$LIB" profile
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ "$output" = "standard" ]
    [[ "$stderr" == *'unknown loa.profile "turbo"; using standard'* ]]
    [ "$(bash "$LIB" source 2>/dev/null)" = "invalid" ]
    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria false 2>/dev/null)" = "true" ]
    # A non-string profile is unknown too.
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: [lean]\n' > "$CFG"
    [ "$(bash "$LIB" profile 2>/dev/null)" = "standard" ]
}

@test "PL-8 the cache is written once and rebuilt when the config or profiles.yaml changes" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\n' > "$CFG"
    touch -d '2026-01-01 00:00:00' "$CFG"
    knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x >/dev/null
    [ -f "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE")" = "lean" ]
    # Same stamps → served from the cache: a planted value proves the read path.
    jq '.knobs["decisions.surface_at_session_start"].value = "from-cache"' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE" > "$T/c" && mv "$T/c" "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x)" = "from-cache" ]
    # A config edit with a new mtime rebuilds.
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: full\n' > "$CFG"
    touch -d '2026-01-02 00:00:00' "$CFG"
    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x)" = "true" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE")" = "full" ]
    # A profiles.yaml edit rebuilds too.
    cp "$PROFILES" "$T/profiles.yaml"
    export LOA_PROFILES_FILE="$T/profiles.yaml"
    knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x >/dev/null
    yq -i '.profiles.full["decisions.surface_at_session_start"] = false' "$T/profiles.yaml"
    touch -d '2026-01-03 00:00:00' "$T/profiles.yaml"
    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x)" = "false" ]
}

@test "PL-9 a corrupt or foreign cache file is rebuilt, never trusted" {
    mkdir -p "$T/run"
    echo 'not json' > "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning x)" = "true" ]
    jq -e '.schema_version == 1' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE" >/dev/null
    jq '.id = "other"' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE" > "$T/c" && mv "$T/c" "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning x)" = "true" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.id' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE")" != "other" ]
}

@test "PL-10 a seam config without a cache seam writes no cache (the repository cache is never touched)" {
    unset LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE
    mkdir -p "$T/root/.claude/data"
    cp "$PROFILES" "$T/root/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
    LOA_PROFILE_ROOT="$T/root" run bash "$LIB" knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x
    [ "$output" = "false" ]
    [ ! -e "$T/root/.run/effective-config.json" ]
}

@test "PL-11 overrides lists the explicit profile keys that differ from the profile, sorted" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\nguardrails:\n  input:\n    enabled: true\ndecisions:\n  surface_at_session_start: false\nstructured_handoff:\n  enabled: true\n' > "$CFG"
    run bash "$LIB" overrides
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ "$output" = "$(printf 'guardrails.input.enabled=true\nstructured_handoff.enabled=true')" ]
}

@test "PL-12 a profiles.yaml key that names a floor key is ignored with a WARN" {
    cp "$PROFILES" "$T/profiles.yaml"
    yq -i '.profiles.standard["implement_gate.mode"] = "deny" | .profiles.standard["flatline_protocol"] = false' "$T/profiles.yaml"
    export LOA_PROFILES_FILE="$T/profiles.yaml"
    run --separate-stderr bash "$LIB" knob implement_gate.mode ask
    [ "$output" = "ask" ]
    [[ "$stderr" == *"profiles.yaml key implement_gate.mode names a floor key; ignored"* ]]
    [[ "$stderr" == *"profiles.yaml key flatline_protocol names a floor key; ignored"* ]]
    [ "$(jq -r '.profile_keys | index("implement_gate.mode")' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE")" = "null" ]
}

@test "PL-13 a malformed key path returns 2 with the fallback and never reaches yq" {
    printf 'a: 1\n' > "$CFG"
    run bash "$LIB" knob '.a | env' fb
    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"fb"* ]]
    run bash "$LIB" knob 'a;b' fb
    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
}

@test "PL-14 the /loa Profile line prints the profile and the explicit overrides" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\nguardrails:\n  input:\n    enabled: true\n' > "$CFG"
    unset LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE
    run --separate-stderr env CACHE_DIR="$T/wscache" LOA_STATUS_RUN_DIR="$T/srun" LOA_STATUS_ENV_DIR="$T/env" \
        LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE="$CFG" timeout 120 bash "$R/.claude/scripts/loa-status.sh" --no-stale-check
    line=$(printf '%s\n' "$output" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep '^Profile:')
    [ "$line" = "Profile: lean (explicit overrides: guardrails.input.enabled=true)" ]
    : > "$CFG"
    run --separate-stderr env CACHE_DIR="$T/wscache" LOA_STATUS_RUN_DIR="$T/srun" LOA_STATUS_ENV_DIR="$T/env" \
        LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE="$CFG" timeout 120 bash "$R/.claude/scripts/loa-status.sh" --no-stale-check
    line=$(printf '%s\n' "$output" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep '^Profile:')
    [ "$line" = "Profile: standard (explicit overrides: none)" ]
}

@test "PL-15 the guardrail readers route through loa_knob (knob on and off)" {
    printf 'guardrails:\n  input:\n    enabled: false\n' > "$CFG"
    run bash "$R/.claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh" --skill implementing-tasks --input "Implement feature X"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.reason')" = "guardrails disabled in config" ]
    printf 'guardrails:\n  input:\n    enabled: true\n' > "$CFG"
    run bash "$R/.claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh" --skill implementing-tasks --input "Implement feature X"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.reason')" != "guardrails disabled in config" ]
    printf 'guardrails:\n  danger_level:\n    enforce: false\n' > "$CFG"
    run bash "$R/.claude/scripts/danger-level-enforcer.sh" --skill deploying-infrastructure --mode autonomous
    [[ "$output" == *"danger level enforcement disabled in config"* ]]
    printf 'guardrails:\n  danger_level:\n    enforce: true\n' > "$CFG"
    run bash "$R/.claude/scripts/danger-level-enforcer.sh" --skill deploying-infrastructure --mode autonomous
    [[ "$output" != *"danger level enforcement disabled in config"* ]]
}

@test "PL-16 the SessionStart readers resolve their enable key through the profile" {
    # `full` turns the decisions and KF surfaces on without their keys; an
    # explicit false beats the profile; `standard` leaves them off.
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: full\n' > "$CFG"
    run bash "$R/.claude/hooks/session-start/loa-decisions-surface.sh"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"[DECISIONS]"* ]]
    run bash "$R/.claude/hooks/loa-kf-surface.sh"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"[KF-SURFACE]"* ]]
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: full\ndecisions:\n  surface_at_session_start: false\nknown_failures:\n  surface_at_session_start: false\n' > "$CFG"
    run bash "$R/.claude/hooks/session-start/loa-decisions-surface.sh"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ -z "$output" ]
    run bash "$R/.claude/hooks/loa-kf-surface.sh"

# (#961 K-1 / FR-1)
#
# PostToolUse:Write|Edit|NotebookEdit hook. Reads tool_input JSON from stdin,
# accumulates session diff lines at .run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl, and emits
# a `[karpathy-surgical-warn]` stderr line + trajectory event when the running
# total exceeds `karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task` (default 100).
#
# Non-blocking by design — returns 0 regardless. The `enforce: block` config
# semantic is RESERVED for v2; v1 honors `warn` only to avoid surprise breakage
# during initial rollout. See grimoires/loa/sdd.md §3.3 + §7 R-3.
#
# Safety invariants (NFR-Sec-1):
#   - tool_input.content / tool_input.new_string NEVER written to state or
#     trajectory. Only line counts + file paths are recorded.
#   - file_path is JSON-escaped inside jq (tojson — the same encoder the old
#     `jq --arg` path used) — no shell-injection vector.
#   - Hook MUST exit 0 even when yq/jq are missing or config is malformed
#     (graceful degradation; never break Write/Edit due to hook env issues).

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
+# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
+#
+# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
+# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
+# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
+# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
+# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
+# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
+# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
+# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
+#
+# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
+# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
+#
+# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
+# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+ROOT="."
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
+command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
+[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
+# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
+# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
+alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
+pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
+
+hits=$(cd "$ROOT" && grep -rnE "$pattern" .claude tools 2>/dev/null \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?tools/check-knob-readers\.sh:' || true)
+if [[ -n "$hits" ]]; then
+  echo "check-knob-readers.sh: direct read(s) of a profile key; use loa_knob from .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:" >&2
+  printf '%s\n' "$hits" | cut -c1-240 >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no direct profile-key reads ($(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') keys checked)"

# cycle-129 FR-9 (SDD D-9.3): one Profile line — the effective loa.profile and
# the explicit keys whose value differs from it. Reads the config the Providers
# block reads (bats-gated seam LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE); the lib runs in a
# subshell so its globals stay out of this script.
display_profile_line() {
  local lib="$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/profile-lib.sh" cfg line
  if [[ ! -f "$lib" ]]; then
    echo -e "${BOLD}Profile:${NC} unknown (lib/profile-lib.sh missing; reinstall the framework with /update-loa)"
    return 0
  fi
  cfg=$(_providers_config_file)
  line=$(
    if [[ "$cfg" != "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then export LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$cfg"; fi
    # shellcheck source=lib/profile-lib.sh
    source "$lib" || exit 0
    name=$(loa_profile 2>/dev/null) || name=standard
    note=""
    if [[ "$(loa_profile_source 2>/dev/null)" == "invalid" ]]; then note="unknown loa.profile, using standard; "; fi
    ov=$(loa_profile_overrides 2>/dev/null | awk 'NF { printf "%s%s", (n++ ? ", " : ""), $0 }')
    printf '%s (%sexplicit overrides: %s)' "${name:-standard}" "$note" "${ov:-none}"
  ) || line=""
  echo -e "${BOLD}Profile:${NC} ${line:-standard (explicit overrides: unavailable)}"
  return 0
}

command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
[[ -f "$CONFIG" ]] || exit 0

# --- master switch and threshold (loa_knob: explicit key > profile > fallback)
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
if [[ "$CONFIG" != "$DEFAULT_CONFIG" ]]; then export LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$CONFIG"; fi
switch="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning true 2>/dev/null)"
case "$switch" in
    false|False|FALSE|0|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) exit 0 ;;
esac
THRESHOLD="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task 100 2>/dev/null)"
[[ "$THRESHOLD" =~ ^[0-9]{1,9}$ ]] || THRESHOLD=100
THRESHOLD=$((10#$THRESHOLD))

# --- payload: one jq, one JSON-encoded field per line (no raw newlines) ---
payload="$(cat)"
[[ -n "$payload" ]] || exit 0
fields="$(printf '%s' "$payload" | jq -r '
    def slines: if . == "" then 1 else (split("\n") | length) end;
    def jl: if type == "array" or type == "object"
            then (if length == 0 then 1 else 2 + ([.[] | jl] | add) end)
            else 1 end;
    def count: if . == null or . == false then 0 elif type == "string" then slines else jl end;

#!/usr/bin/env bats
bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/run-checkpoint-derive.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 2 Task 2.10
# (PRD FR-5 AC-5.1 … AC-5.4, FR-4(f) AC-4.6; SDD D-5.1, D-5.1a, D-5.2, D-5.3, D-5.4)
# `run-checkpoint.sh derive` rebuilds the run position from files: one case per
# decision-table row, the breaker recompute from the feedback history, the
# write path and its rollback knob, and one case per known reader over a
# derived file. Fixture: a tiny git repo with a ledger, a2a/ and .run/ in a
# temp dir; nothing touches this checkout's .run/.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
  CK="$REPO/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rcd.XXXXXX")"
  R="$T/repo"
  mkdir -p "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a" "$R/.run" "$R/src"
  git -C "$R" init -q
  printf 'x\n' > "$R/src/a.ts"
  git -C "$R" add -A
  git -C "$R" -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@example.invalid commit -qm "feat: impl"
  ledger completed completed completed
  unset LOA_RUN_DIR LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE
}
teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }

# ledger STATUS101 STATUS102 STATUS103 [EXTRA-SPRINT-JSON]
ledger() {
  jq -n --arg a "$1" --arg b "$2" --arg c "$3" --argjson x "${4:-null}" '
    {schema_version: 1, active_cycle: "cycle-x", next_sprint_number: 104,
     cycles: [
       {id: "cycle-old", status: "archived", created: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        sprints: [{global_id: 1, local_label: "sprint-1", status: "completed", created: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]},
       {id: "cycle-x", status: "active", created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        sprints: ([{global_id: 101, local_label: "sprint-1", status: $a, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
                   {global_id: 102, local_label: "sprint-2", status: $b, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
                   {global_id: 103, local_label: "sprint-3", status: $c, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]
                  + (if $x == null then [] else [$x] end))}]}' > "$R/grimoires/loa/ledger.json"
}

# feedback GID GATE VERDICT [SPRINT_ID] [ROUND] [MEDIUM] [TS] — a feedback file whose trailer verdict-derive accepts
feedback() {
  local gid="$1" gate="$2" verdict="$3" sid="${4:-sprint-$1}" round="${5:-}" med="${6:-0}" ts="${7:-2026-06-01T00:00:00Z}" f prose
  mkdir -p "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$gid"
  if [[ "$gate" == review ]]; then f=engineer-feedback; else f=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
  [[ -n "$round" ]] && f="$f-r$round"
  if [[ "$verdict" == APPROVED ]]; then
    if [[ "$gate" == review ]]; then prose='All good'; else prose="APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO"; fi
  else
    prose=$'# Feedback\n\n## Findings\n\n- MEDIUM: something to fix'
  fi
  printf '%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":%s,"low":0},"sprint_id":"%s","ts":"%s"} -->\n' \
    "$prose" "$gate" "$verdict" "$med" "$sid" "$ts" > "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$gid/$f.md"
}

# complete GID [SPRINT_ID] — review + audit APPROVED and the COMPLETED marker
complete() {
  feedback "$1" review APPROVED "${2:-}"
  feedback "$1" audit APPROVED "${2:-}"
  printf 'COMPLETED 2026-06-01T00:00:00Z\nsprint: %s\n' "${2:-sprint-$1}" > "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$1/COMPLETED"
}

# cache STATE [AGE_HOURS] [EXTRA-JQ] — .run/sprint-plan-state.json (jq now: portable, no GNU date -d)
cache() {
  jq -n --arg s "$1" --argjson h "${2:-0}" '
    {schema_version: 2, plan_id: "plan-x", branch: "feature/x", state: $s,
     timestamps: {started: "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z", last_activity: (now - $h * 3600 | floor | todate)},
     sprints: {total: 3, completed: 0, current: "sprint-1",
               list: [{id: "sprint-1", status: "in_progress"}, {id: "sprint-2", status: "pending"}, {id: "sprint-3", status: "pending"}]}}
    '"${3:+| $3}" > "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"

content.text:
I found four real defects in the heredoc classifier: two that let a check the fence makes today stop happening, and two coverage or doc gaps. The full corpus passes in a scratch copy under bash 5.2 (benign 89/89, dangerous 142/142). For each finding I compared the new classifier (knob on) against `heredoc_classifier: false` (knob off, the old scan) on crafted inputs, and every case below blocks with the knob off but is allowed with it on. A safety classifier interrupted one turn, and Bash access was then denied, so a few planned checks didn't run (listed at the end).

### Findings

1. **A heredoc written to a file and then run in the same command by piping or process-substituting that file into a shell is classified as non-executing.** — `pr/head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:608-639`, decisive check at line 631.
   - `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` judges each pipeline member on its own, splitting on `|`, `(` and `)`. The member that names the file is a "safe reader" such as `cat`, and the member that is a shell never names the file, so it returns "not executed".
   - Wildcard spellings of the target (line 625) or commands that run the file without naming it (npm, make, git hooks via `core.hooksPath`) are missed in the same way.
   - This contradicts the PR's claim that a file written and then executed later in the same command is caught; only a separate tool call is a documented gap. Confidence: high.

2. **Body lines whose command follows a shell keyword are dropped, not kept for the normal rules.** — `pr/head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:546-567` (`_bdb_hd_segword`).
   - Only `(`, `{`, `!`, a backslash, quotes, assignments and a list of wrappers are stripped. `if`, `then`, `do`, `else`, `elif`, `while` and `until` are not, so the segment's command word becomes the keyword and the fence-verb segment is discarded at lines 589-597.
   - The block comment (lines ~160-170) and `hooks-reference.md` say segments whose command word is a fence verb are kept. In shell grammar the verb after the keyword *is* the command word.
   - On its own this only matters if the body later runs. Combined with finding 1 it is a confirmed same-command allow that blocks with the knob off. Confidence: high.

3. **Only a short verb list survives the body scan.** — `pr/head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:214-220`.
   - `_bdb_hd_is_destructive` covers rm, git, find, dd, shred, truncate, kubectl, terraform, aws, gcloud, psql, mysql, mkfs and the SQL keywords.
   - The fence's System Zone rules (FR-SZ / FR-SZ2: cp, mv, ln, tee, `sed -i`, tar into `.claude/` or state paths) rely on words not in that list. Their body segments are therefore dropped and those rules never see them.
   - That is harmless while the body really stays data, but with finding 1 it is a confirmed regression: a body that copies over a `.claude/hooks/` file is allowed with the knob on and blocked with it off.
   - The comment says the fence verb list is "Command words the fence's own rules match", which is incomplete. Confidence: high (verified empirically).

4. **The executable-target list misses common auto-run locations.** — `pr/head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:190` (`_bdb_hd_re_sys`).
   - `.husky/*` (git hooks via `core.hooksPath`), `node_modules/.bin/*`, `package.json` scripts, `Makefile` and `.github/workflows/*` are all treated as plain files.
   - The `s?bin/` rule requires a `/` or start of string before `bin`, so `.bin/x` isn't matched.
   - The docs' wording ("executable content") suggests broader coverage. Confidence: medium (the npm case was verified as allowed with the knob on and blocked with it off).

5. **The guard-yield test change can't detect whether the classifier is wired in, and nothing in the PR wires it in.** — `pr/head/tests/unit/guard-yield.bats:34` and `pr/head/.claude/scripts/lib/heredoc-classifier.sh:6,14`.
   - The lib's header says `guard-yield.sh` calls `heredoc_nonexec`, but `.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh` is not among the PR's 68 changed files.
   - The only fixture row is a benign non-executing heredoc that the old "`<<` present" fallback also classes as a likely false positive. With no interpreter-heredoc row expected to count as real, GY-3 (line 85) passes either way.
   - The comment "FR-6 classifier via lib/heredoc-classifier.sh" is therefore unverified. Confidence: medium-high.

6. **The corpus has no row covering findings 1–3.** — `pr/head/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl` (rows D119–D121).
   - The same-line execution rows only test the target named directly as a shell argument, `chmod +x` then `./x`, and `source x`.
   - No row pipes or process-substitutes the target into a shell, prefixes a body verb with a keyword, or puts a non-listed fence-rule verb in the body.
   - So "dangerous 142/142" does not cover the fail-closed claims for those paths. Confidence: high.

### Checked and not defective
- Library mode applies only when the file is sourced, not executed (`block-destructive-bash.sh:762`), so the environment variable can't switch the fence off.
- The tokenizer fails closed on open quotes, trailing backslashes and comments.
- Multiple heredocs on one header, variable delimiters, missing terminators, control characters, `$(`, backticks, `<(` / `>(` and nested `<<` all fall back to the full scan.
- `jq`/`yq -i` (D114/D115) and the `sed -n` print-only regex are handled correctly.
- The quoted standalone `cat` special case behaves the same as the old #1245 scrub.

### Not completed
I meant to test knob parsing variants (tab indentation, a flow-style `{heredoc_classifier: false}` mapping) and finish a doc-versus-code pass on `pr/head/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md`. From reading the code, a flow-style mapping is not recognised, so the classifier stays on when the user meant to turn it off. That is a minor, unverified point.

2. **Body lines whose command follows a shell keyword are dropped, not kept for the normal rules.** — `pr/head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:546-567` (`_bdb_hd_segword`).

   - On its own this only matters if the body later runs. Combined with finding 1 it is a confirmed same-command allow that blocks with the knob off. Confidence: high.

3. **Only a short verb list survives the body scan.** — `pr/head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:214-220`.

   - The `s?bin/` rule requires a `/` or start of string before `bin`, so `.bin/x` isn't matched.
   - The docs' wording ("executable content") suggests broader coverage. Confidence: medium (the npm case was verified as allowed with the knob on and blocked with it off).

   - The same-line execution rows only test the target named directly as a shell argument, `chmod +x` then `./x`, and `source x`.

   - So "dangerous 142/142" does not cover the fail-closed claims for those paths. Confidence: high.

- The tokenizer fails closed on open quotes, trailing backslashes and comments.
- Multiple heredocs on one header, variable delimiters, missing terminators, control characters, `$(`, backticks, `<(` / `>(` and nested `<<` all fall back to the full scan.
- `jq`/`yq -i` (D114/D115) and the `sed -n` print-only regex are handled correctly.
- The quoted standalone `cat` special case behaves the same as the old #1245 scrub.

I meant to test knob parsing variants (tab indentation, a flow-style `{heredoc_classifier: false}` mapping) and finish a doc-versus-code pass on `pr/head/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md`. From reading the code, a flow-style mapping is not recognised, so the classifier stays on when the user meant to turn it off. That is a minor, unverified point.

content.text:
I found five real defects in the profile system, the worst being a cache that can hand back stale values after you edit the config. The snapshot affects verification: `pr/head/` holds only the 68 changed files, so `.claude/data/floor.yaml` and `tests/unit/guard-origins.bats` are in neither `head/` nor `base/`. `base/.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml:23` already refers to `floor.yaml floor_guards`, so `floor.yaml` most likely exists in the full repo unchanged; I couldn't confirm that.

Test runs: in a scratch copy at `/tmp/review-p/head` with mikefarah yq v4.40.5 and GNU coreutils 9.1, `profile-lib.bats` passed 13 of 17. PL-8 and PL-12 fail only because `floor.yaml` is missing, and both pass once I add a plausible one. PL-14 and PL-15 fail because other scripts (`time-lib.sh`, `workflow-state.sh`) aren't in the snapshot. I didn't run `profile-floor.bats` for the same reason.

What checks out:
- **Resolution order is correct.** An explicit `false` wins over `full`, an unset key takes the profile value, other keys fall back, an explicit `null` counts as unset, and an unknown, non-string or wrong-case profile warns and uses `standard`. A bad path returns 2 with the fallback, and a leading dot is accepted.
- **All consumers call it correctly.** They use `loa_knob KEY FALLBACK` in the right order and the skill prose uses `profile-lib.sh knob KEY FALLBACK`. The file is mode 100755 and sourcing it changes no shell options.
- **Most `standard` values match the old defaults.** Comparing each consumer's old default in `base/` against the `standard` value, `known_failures`, `decisions`, `structured_handoff`, `soul_identity_doc`, `surgical_diff_warning` and `require_success_criteria` all match.
- **The guardrail default flips are intended and documented** (DEC-0161; the example shows `true`→`false` for `guardrails.input.enabled` and `guardrails.danger_level.enforce`). The old `// true` also meant an explicit `false` was silently read as `true`, which the PR fixes.

## Findings

**1. Cache key loses mtime and size on Linux when any input file is missing** — `pr/head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:77-78`. Confidence: high that it happens; how often depends on whether `floor.yaml` ships.
- If one of the three files is missing, GNU `stat -Lc` exits 1. The macOS fallback `stat -Lf` then runs, but on GNU `-f` means filesystem status. It prints free-block and inode counts, with no mtime or size.
- The cache key is then built from disk-usage numbers: it misses when disk usage moves and serves stale values when it doesn't. The guard at line 79 ("empty stat output disables caching") never fires, because the output isn't empty.
- I reproduced it on the real lib with `floor.yaml` absent: after `yq -i '.decisions.surface_at_session_start = true' .loa.config.yaml`, `knob` still printed `false` until I deleted `.run/effective-config.json`. With a `floor.yaml` present the same edit is picked up.
- This is also why PL-8 fails in the snapshot.

**2. A missing `floor.yaml` silently turns off floor protection** — `pr/head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:109-111`. Confidence: high.
- If the file is absent, the floor list is just `[]`, with no warning. A missing `profiles.yaml` does warn (lines 101-108).
- `LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE=/nonexistent` does the same, and none of the `LOA_PROFILE_*` overrides at lines 61-64 are restricted to bats runs.
- Reproduced via PL-12 in the snapshot: an injected `implement_gate.mode: deny` in the profile resolved to `deny`.
- Practical impact is limited because floor readers don't go through `loa_knob`, but "no profile can reach the floor" then rests on that alone.

**3. Floor-key matching has two gaps** — `pr/head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:124`. Confidence: high (both reproduced); severity: low.
- An ancestor of a pattern with a `*` in the middle isn't caught. With floor key `flatline_protocol.*.companion_voice`, a profile key `flatline_protocol.code_review` resolved to its profile value.
- A child of an exact floor key isn't caught either. With floor key `hounfour.locality`, a profile key `hounfour.locality.mode` resolved.
- PF-2 in `pr/head/tests/unit/profile-floor.bats:56-57` uses the same logic, so it can't detect either case.

**4. `standard` turns `invisible_retrospective` on for configs that don't set it** — `pr/head/.claude/data/profiles.yaml:42`. Confidence: medium.
- The old skill-include (`base/.claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md:1`) ran the scan only on an explicit `true`. The PR's own fixture (`standard-oracle.json`) records `empty_config_today: false` and `this_repo_today: false`, against `standard: true`.
- So any config without the key, including this repo's `.loa.config.yaml`, which doesn't set it, flips from off to on. Only the two guardrail keys are documented as migration items.
- It's ambiguous: the old `continuous-learning/resources/retrospective-postlude.md` exited only on an explicit `false`. Either way the change should be called out.
- PL-4 doesn't catch it because it compares against the example file, which sets `true`.

**5. `/loa` Profile line passes override values through `echo -e`** — `pr/head/.claude/scripts/loa-status.sh:960`. Confidence: high on mechanism; severity: low.
- The overrides are control-stripped by `clean()`, but `echo -e` then interprets literal backslash escapes. A config string like `"\e[2J"` becomes a real terminal escape, which defeats the stripping the lib header promises. `printf '%s'` would fix it.

## Lower-impact notes

- **Python yq (kislyuk) is not supported** — `pr/head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:96`, medium confidence, not tested (I couldn't install it). `yq -o=json` is mikefarah-only. With the Python `yq` on PATH the whole config would count as unparseable, so explicit keys would be ignored and only profile defaults applied. The old `yq -r '.k // d'` reads in the orchestrator and enforcer worked with either. Only `loa-decisions-surface.sh` checks for yq v4 (`have_yq4`); the kf, l6, l7, orchestrator and enforcer callers don't.
- **No fallback in the retrospective include** — `pr/head/.claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md:1` calls `knob invisible_retrospective.enabled` with no fallback. If the lib can't resolve (jq or yq missing) it prints an empty string and the scan is skipped. `continuous-learning/resources/retrospective-postlude.md:34` passes `true` for the same key, so the two disagree.

## Tests

Apart from the gaps noted above (PF-2 under finding 3, PL-4 under finding 4), the tests assert what they claim. PL-3 only compares two hand-written files from the same PR (`profiles.yaml` against the oracle fixture), so it guards against drift rather than proving the old defaults.

I found two real logic bugs in how the hook picks its key. Both are caused by how `run-checkpoint.sh read --json` works, and I reproduced both. The rest of the documented contract holds. All 21 tests pass in a scratch copy at `/home/evaluser/review-k`, because `/tmp` is mounted noexec here. To run them I restored the exec bit, which the snapshot dropped (the diff says 100755), and replaced the `local REDACTED-TEST-SECRET"` lines, which the snapshot redacted and which otherwise break bats parsing. Neither of those is a PR defect.

**Bugs**

1. **The per-task key points at the previous task** (`pr/head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:129-136`, doc at 8-14; `pr/head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:220`). High confidence, reproduced.
   - `run-checkpoint.sh read` only returns `.checkpoint.task` once beads confirms that bead is closed (`run-checkpoint.sh:198-208`; `state-schemas.md:107`: "`task` is the last CLOSED bead"). So the key is always the last finished task, not the one being worked on.
   - Simulated flow: sprint start → 3 lines, close A → 4 lines, close B → 2 lines. Result: `sprint-1.jsonl`=3 (A's work), `bd-A.jsonl`=4 (B's work), `bd-B.jsonl`=2 (review-phase writes).
   - The SURGICAL axis reads `.run/karpathy-surgical/<bead>.jsonl` per sprint bead, so it reports the next task's lines against each bead. The summary's `task` label is wrong in the same way.
   - KS-1 and KS-3 use a fake `br` that reports "closed" and treat that task as the current one, so the tests lock in the wrong behaviour instead of catching it.

2. **A finished run's checkpoint is used forever** (`karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:130-134`, with `run-checkpoint.sh:187-211`). High confidence, reproduced.
   - `cmd_read` never checks `.state`, and `sprint-plan-state.json` is kept after a run (it is set to `JACKED_OUT`, not deleted).
   - Every later interactive session therefore adds to the last bead's file instead of falling back to its session id. With `JACKED_OUT` and new session ids `newsession1`/`newsession2`, both writes went into `bd-B.jsonl`, running total 4.
   - The total never resets, so once it passes the threshold every Write/Edit in every later session warns and writes a trajectory event. No test covers this.

3. **NotebookEdit is never counted** (`karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:95,97`). Medium-high confidence; this is carried over from base. It reads `.tool_input.new_string` and `.tool_input.file_path`, but Claude Code's NotebookEdit sends `new_source` and `notebook_path`. Every NotebookEdit records 0 lines with file `<unknown>`. The header (line 7) and the matcher claim it is covered.

4. **Text ending in a newline counts one extra line** (`karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:86`). Low-medium confidence; matches base behaviour. `slines` returns `split("\n")|length`, so `"a\nb\n"` counts 3 (checked). An empty `new_string` (a pure deletion) counts 1. Most Writes end in a newline, so most are overcounted by 1.

**Symlink and race gaps (low)**

5. **Summary and trajectory writes follow symlinks** (`karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:182-185, 205`). The temp file `$SUMMARY.tmp.$$` has a predictable name and is written with `>`, which follows a planted symlink. `mv` onto a symlink that points to a directory moves the temp file into that directory. The trajectory `>>` also follows symlinks. The doc only promises refusal for the state directory and state file, so this is a gap rather than a contradiction.

6. **Check-then-write race** (`karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:153` vs `164`). The `-L` check and the `>>` append are separate steps. A FIFO planted at the task path would make the hook block.

**Minor (low)**

7. **NUL in `session_id` reaches stderr** (`karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:124`). A `\u0000` makes bash print "ignored null byte in input" to stderr. The exit code is still 0.

8. **`KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP` with a leading zero** (`karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:64`). `08` prints "value too great for base" to stderr. `010` is read as octal 8. This only affects the test seam.

9. **Legacy cleanup never runs when the knob is off** (`karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:74-77` run before 141-147). The early exit comes first, so under the `lean` profile `.run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl` is never deleted, contrary to "deleted on the first run". The perf-cache deletion only happens with the default state directory, which KS-6 never uses, so that branch is untested.

10. **Warning text still says "Session diff total"** (`karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:193`). The count is now per task (or per previous task, see 1). KS-4 pins this wording.

**Confirmed working**
- Sanitisation: allowed characters only, leading dot → `_`, 128-byte cut, no path traversal.
- Rotation keeps exactly KEEP files and never deletes the current one.
- The summary write is atomic and has exactly the five documented keys.
- Payload content never appears in state, summary or trajectory.
- No stdout and exit 0 across all the malformed payloads I tried.
- The `lean` profile turns the hook off, and an explicit `true` overrides it.

Each Write/Edit now also starts `run-checkpoint.sh` and `br show`, about 300ms per call measured without `br`. This is not a correctness problem.

    status_cfg="${LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE:-}"

  _LOA_PL_CFG="${LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE:-${status_cfg:-$default_cfg}}"
  _LOA_PL_PROF="${LOA_PROFILES_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/profiles.yaml}"
  _LOA_PL_FLOOR="${LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/floor.yaml}"
  if [[ -n "${LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE:-}" ]]; then

head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:631 — The fail-closed claim does not hold: `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` judges each pipeline segment on its own, so a heredoc written to a plain file and then fed to a shell in the same command (`cat > notes.txt <<'EOF' … EOF` then `cat notes.txt | bash`, or `sh <(cat notes.txt)`) is classed non-executing. The segment that names the file is a "safe reader" and the `bash` segment never names it. Reproduced: a body `if true; then rm -rf /home/user; fi` piped to bash is allowed (exit 0) with the classifier on and BLOCKED [FR-2-BLOCK] with `heredoc_classifier: false`, so this is a regression against the old scan.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:538 — `_bdb_hd_segword` strips `(`, `{`, `!`, quotes, assignments and wrappers but not shell keywords (`if`/`then`/`do`/`else`/`elif`/`while`/`until`). A body segment like `then rm -rf …` therefore gets command word `then`, and its fence verb is discarded instead of kept for the normal rules, contrary to the block comment and hooks-reference.md ("segments that start with a fence verb are kept").
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:214 — `_bdb_hd_is_destructive` ("command words the fence's own rules match") omits the verbs behind the System-Zone rules (cp, mv, ln, tee, sed -i, tar, chmod, …). Those body segments of a non-executing heredoc are dropped and FR-SZ/FR-SZ2 never see them. Reproduced together with the pipe case: a body `cp evil.sh .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh` then `cat notes.txt | sh` is allowed with the classifier on and BLOCKED [FR-SZ2-COPY] with it off.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:190 — The executable-target regex misses common auto-run locations (`.husky/*` via core.hooksPath, `node_modules/.bin/*`, Makefile, package.json scripts, `.github/workflows/*`; the `s?bin/` arm requires `/` or start-of-string before `bin`, so `.bin/x` does not match). A body written there is treated as plain data, although the docs describe this class as "executable content".
head/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl:236 — The new FR-6 corpus rows cover only a target named directly as a shell argument, `chmod +x`/`./x` and `source x`. No row pipes or process-substitutes the target into a shell, prefixes a body verb with a keyword, or puts a System-Zone verb in the body, so the green corpus does not support the "fail-closed" claim for the paths above.
head/tests/unit/guard-yield.bats:34 — The fixture change claims to exercise "FR-6 classifier via lib/heredoc-classifier.sh", but guard-yield.sh is not in this change and the only row is a benign heredoc that the old "`<<` present" fallback already classes as likely-FP. GY-3 passes whether or not the classifier is wired in; heredoc-classifier.sh:6 documents a caller that this PR never adds.
head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:131 — The per-task key comes from `run-checkpoint.sh read --json` `.checkpoint.task`, but `read` returns a task only once beads confirms it closed, and /implement checkpoints on each `br close`. The key is therefore always the previously finished bead, not the current one. Each `.run/karpathy-surgical/<bead>.jsonl` collects the next task's lines (and the sprint file collects the first task's), so the reviewer's SURGICAL axis (reviewing-code/SKILL.md:220) attributes diff sizes to the wrong bead. KS-1/KS-3 stub `br` as closed and encode the wrong behaviour.
head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:130 — `cmd_read` ignores the run state, and `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` survives a run as JACKED_OUT. Every later interactive session keeps keying its writes to the last bead of the finished run instead of falling back to the session id. That total never resets, so once it passes the threshold every Write/Edit in every later session warns and appends a trajectory event. No test covers a finished run.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:77 — If any of the three inputs is missing (no .loa.config.yaml, or no floor.yaml), GNU `stat -Lc` exits 1 and the BSD fallback `stat -Lf` runs. On GNU `-f` means filesystem status, so it prints block/inode counts and no mtime or size. The cache key stops tracking edits, the "empty stat disables caching" guard never fires, and edits to the remaining files are served stale from .run/effective-config.json (confirmed: GNU `stat -Lf` prints filesystem stats and exits 1).
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:109 — A missing or unreadable floor.yaml (or `LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE` pointed elsewhere; the seam is not bats-gated) silently gives an empty floor list with no WARN. Any profile key, including a floor key such as implement_gate.mode, then resolves through the profile, so "no profile can reach the floor" fails open. A missing profiles.yaml, by contrast, does warn.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:124 — `forbidden()` misses a child of an exact floor key (floor `a.b`, profile key `a.b.c`) and an ancestor of a pattern with a mid-path `*` (floor `x.*.y`, profile key `x.z`). profile-floor.bats PF-2 reuses the same logic, so it cannot catch either case.
head/.claude/data/profiles.yaml:42 — `standard` sets `invisible_retrospective.enabled: true`. The old include ran the retrospective only on an explicit `true`, so every config without the key (this repository's .loa.config.yaml included) silently switches it on. The PR's own standard-oracle.json records the current value as false, and only the two guardrail keys are documented as migration items.
head/.claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md:1 — The include calls `profile-lib.sh knob invisible_retrospective.enabled` with no fallback (the CLI is `knob <path> <fallback>`), while continuous-learning/resources/retrospective-postlude.md:34 passes `true` for the same key. When the lib cannot resolve (jq/yq missing) the include prints empty and skips, and the two procedures disagree.
head/.claude/scripts/loa-status.sh:960 — The Profile line is printed with `echo -e`. Override values from the config are control-stripped by the lib, but a literal backslash sequence such as `\e[2J` in a config string is then turned into a real terminal escape, which undoes the sanitisation; print the line with printf '%s'.
head/.claude/scripts/test-lint-invariants.sh:257 — The good-fixture assertions are loosened from exit 0 to "0 or 1", so a regression that adds a new WARN to a clean tree no longer fails the self-test. The environment-dependent WARNs should be stubbed in the fixture rather than accepted wholesale.

On GNU `-f` means filesystem status, so it prints block/inode counts and no mtime or size. The cache key stops tracking edits, the "empty stat disables caching" guard never fires, and edits to the remaining files are served stale from .run/effective-config.json (confirmed: GNU `stat -Lf` prints filesystem stats and exits 1).
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:109 — A missing or unreadable floor.yaml (or `LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE` pointed elsewhere; the seam is not bats-gated) silently gives an empty floor list with no WARN. Any profile key, including a floor key such as implement_gate.mode, then resolves through the profile, so "no profile can reach the floor" fails open. A missing profiles.yaml, by contrast, does warn.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:124 — `forbidden()` misses a child of an exact floor key (floor `a.b`, profile key `a.b.c`) and an ancestor of a pattern with a mid-path `*` (floor `x.*.y`, profile key `x.z`). profile-floor.bats PF-2 reuses the same logic, so it cannot catch either case.
head/.claude/data/profiles.yaml:42 — `standard` sets `invisible_retrospective.enabled: true`. The old include ran the retrospective only on an explicit `true`, so every config without the key (this repository's .loa.config.yaml included) silently switches it on. The PR's own standard-oracle.json records the current value as false, and only the two guardrail keys are documented as migration items.
head/.claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md:1 — The include calls `profile-lib.sh knob invisible_retrospective.enabled` with no fallback (the CLI is `knob <path> <fallback>`), while continuous-learning/resources/retrospective-postlude.md:34 passes `true` for the same key. When the lib cannot resolve (jq/yq missing) the include prints empty and skips, and the two procedures disagree.
head/.claude/scripts/loa-status.sh:960 — The Profile line is printed with `echo -e`. Override values from the config are control-stripped by the lib, but a literal backslash sequence such as `\e[2J` in a config string is then turned into a real terminal escape, which undoes the sanitisation; print the line with printf '%s'.
head/.claude/scripts/test-lint-invariants.sh:257 — The good-fixture assertions are loosened from exit 0 to "0 or 1", so a regression that adds a new WARN to a clean tree no longer fails the self-test. The environment-dependent WARNs should be stubbed in the fixture rather than accepted wholesale.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

I've written the review to `/workspace/review.md`: 15 findings and **Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED**.

**Why it can't merge:** the "fail-closed heredoc classifier" fails open in a case the old scan blocked, in `block-destructive-bash.sh`. Write a heredoc to a plain file, then pipe that file into a shell in the same command. If the body is `if true; then rm -rf /home/user; fi`, or a `cp` over a `.claude/hooks/` file, the command is allowed with the classifier on and blocked with `heredoc_classifier: false`. I ran both cases against the hook. Three causes combine:
- Each pipeline segment is judged on its own, so `cat notes.txt` counts as a "safe reader".
- A verb after a shell keyword like `then` isn't recognised as a command, so it gets dropped.
- The list of verbs kept from the body leaves out `cp`, `mv`, `tee` and `sed -i`.

The test corpus has no case like this, and the `guard-yield.bats` change passes whether or not the classifier is wired in.

**Other defects:**
- **Karpathy hook (diff-size count per task):**
  - The key is the *last closed* bead, not the current one, because `run-checkpoint.sh read` only reports a task once beads says it's closed. So diff sizes are charged to the wrong bead.
  - A finished run's checkpoint keeps being used in later sessions, so that total never resets and warns forever once it passes the threshold.
- **Profiles (`profile-lib.sh`):**
  - If any input file is missing, the cache stops noticing edits and serves stale values. On Linux the fallback `stat -Lf` prints filesystem stats with no mtime or size; I confirmed that output.
  - A missing `floor.yaml` silently removes floor protection, with no warning.
  - Floor-key matching misses child and wildcard-ancestor keys.
  - The `standard` profile quietly turns on `invisible_retrospective` for configs that never set it, including this repo's own config.
- **Lower severity:**
  - The retrospective include calls the profile lookup with no fallback value.
  - The `/loa` Profile line uses `echo -e`, which can turn config text into terminal escapes.
  - The lint self-test now accepts warnings on the clean fixture, so new warnings no longer fail it.

**What I checked, and what I couldn't run:**
- I verified the heredoc, profile-cache and karpathy findings directly. The rest come from reading the code against base, and from three background agents that reproduced theirs in scratch copies.
- The new implement-gate tests (IG-24 to IG-33) pass, and I found no defect in the gate's mode logic.
- I couldn't get meaningful results from the `run-checkpoint` derive/record-round, lint-invariants or prompt-budget suites. The snapshot lacks `verdict-derive.sh` and test fixtures, dropped exec bits, and `/tmp` is mounted noexec. Those failures are environmental, so `run-checkpoint.sh derive` and `record-round` were reviewed by reading only.
- I didn't flag the guardrail and danger-level enforcement now being off by default. It's a safety reduction, but deliberate and documented (DEC-0161).

for cfg in $'destructive_command_guard:\n  heredoc_classifier: false' $'destructive_command_guard:\n  heredoc_classifier: false   # rollback' $'destructive_command_guard:\n\theredoc_classifier: false' $'destructive_command_guard:  # fence\n  heredoc_classifier: false' $'destructive_command_guard: {heredoc_classifier: false}'; do
  d=$(mktemp -d); printf '%s\n' "$cfg" > $d/.loa.config.yaml
  r=$(LOA_REPO_ROOT=$d bash -c 'BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 source "$1"; _bdb_heredoc_knob_on && echo on || echo off' _ "$H")
  printf '%-60q -> %s\n' "$cfg" "$r"; rm -rf $d
done
grep -n 'BDB_LIB_ONLY' $H | head
